01. 이 질문에 몇 점을 줘야 하죠?: 01. What score should I give this question?
설문 문항과 응답 도구를 직접 바꿔 보는 방법론 실험실: A methods laboratory for changing survey items and response tools
Choose a format, answer it yourself, and ask what the resulting number means.
A/B/C selects a tool or item. Enter the actual response using the control that appears.
02. 좋아하지만, 만들 자신은 없다면?: 02. What if you like AI but lack confidence in creating materials?
가상 강사 민서: AI는 좋아하지만, 초안을 만들 자신은 낮음: Fictional instructor Minseo likes AI but has little confidence in making a draft.
I like generative AI and can make good drafts of teaching materials.
응답 체험 · 정답 없음 · 1·3·5점만 골라 비교: Response exploration · No correct answer · Compare scores of 1, 3, and 5
5점 동의 척도 · 1 전혀 동의 안 함 / 2 동의 안 함 / 3 보통: Five-point agreement scale · 1 Strongly disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Neither agree nor disagree / 4 Agree / 5 Strongly agree
“좋아하는 정도라면 5점이에요.”: “If you mean how much I like it, I would give it a 5.”
Answering based on liking could be mistaken for high confidence in creating materials.
Ask about liking and confidence separately.
“초안을 만드는 건 아직 어려워요.”: “Making a draft is still difficult for me.”
Answering based on confidence could be mistaken for disliking AI.
First define what a single score is supposed to mean.
“좋아하긴 하는데… 중간으로 할게요.”: “I do like it... I will choose the middle.”
3점은 둘 다 보통이라는 뜻일 수도, 두 판단 사이에서 타협한 답일 수도: A 3 could mean that both judgments are moderate, or that the respondent compromised between two different judgments.
The respondent is not wrong. The question combines two judgments.
결론: 점수만으로 호감과 자신감을 구별할 수 없습니다. 다음 개념 구분을: Conclusion: the score alone cannot separate liking from confidence. After distinguishing the concepts, we will split the item in the double-barreled-question laboratory.
판별 문제 · 정답 1개 · A/B/C는 수업 답안: Classification question · One correct answer · A/B/C are classroom answers
This asks for an evaluation of liking or disliking.
Interpret this response as liking AI use. It is not an ability score.
“좋아하지만 이번 주에는 한 번도 안 썼어요.”: “I like it, but I have not used it at all this week.”
Liking and actual frequency of use can differ.
To ask about frequency, specify the time period and unit of use.
“좋아해도 자료를 만들 자신은 없어요.”: “I may like it without feeling confident about making materials.”
Enjoyment alone does not tell us whether someone feels able to complete a task.
Ask about a specific task the respondent believes they can perform.
04. “지난 7일 중 며칠”은 무엇을 재나요?: 04. What does “how many of the past seven days” measure?
지난 7일 동안 강의 준비에 생성형 AI를 사용한 날은 며칠입니까?: On how many of the past seven days did you use generative AI to prepare teaching materials?
사용 일수 · 0–7일 중 정수로 응답 · 0일=사용 안 함, 7일=매일: Days of use · Answer with an integer from 0 to 7 · 0 = no use, 7 = every day; this is not an agreement scale
“좋아하지 않아도 업무 때문에 썼어요.”: “I used it for work even though I do not like it.”
Days of use are not the same as liking.
Ask about liking in a separate evaluative item.
“7일 중 3일 사용했어요.”: “I used it on three of the seven days.”
This measures use behavior with a defined period and counting unit.
It means three days of use, not three points of agreement or ability.
“매일 써도 매번 막혀요.”: “I use it every day but still get stuck.”
Frequent use alone does not establish confidence in creating materials.
Separately ask how strongly the respondent currently believes they can perform a specific task.
05. “만들 수 있다”는 무엇을 재나요?: 05. What does “I can make it” measure?
나는 생성형 AI에 요청하여 수업 주제에 맞는 설명 자료의 초안을 만들: I can ask generative AI to produce a draft explanation suited to the topic of my class.
0–10점 자신감 · 정수 11개 중 선택 · 0 전혀 할 수 없음 /: Confidence from 0 to 10 · Eleven integer options · 0 Cannot do it at all / 5 Moderately certain / 10 Highly certain I can do it
“할 수 있다고 생각했는데, 해보니 어려웠어요.”: “I thought I could do it, but it was difficult when I tried.”
설문은 자신의 믿음을 받았습니다. 실제 수행 결과를 관찰한 것은 아닙니다: The survey collected the respondent’s belief. It did not observe actual performance.
Assessing ability requires a performance task and evaluation criteria.
“할 수는 있지만 다음 수업에는 안 쓸 거예요.”: “I can do it, but I will not use it in my next class.”
Believing that one can do something differs from planning to do it.
Ask about intention separately, for example, “I intend to use it in the future.”
“이 일은 내가 해낼 수 있다고 생각해요.”: “I believe I can accomplish this task.”
This asks about belief in one’s ability to perform a specific task: self-efficacy.
예: 8점은 높은 수행 자신감입니다. 실제 능력 80점이라는 뜻이 아닙니: For example, 8 means high confidence, not an actual ability score of 80.
06. An item needs a response scale.
문항은 묻는 문장, 응답 눈금은 답하는 방식입니다. 숫자를 붙였다고 검증: The item is the question; the response scale is how it is answered. Adding numbers does not create a validated scale.
호감 — 1–5점 동의 — 1 전혀 동의 안 함 ↔ 5 매우 동의함: Liking — Agreement from 1 to 5 — 1 Strongly disagree ↔ 5 Strongly agree
사용 빈도 — 0–7일 — 지난 7일 중 사용한 날 수: Frequency of use — 0 to 7 days — Number of days used in the past seven days
제작 자신감 — 0–10점 — 0 전혀 할 수 없음 ↔ 10 확실히 할: Production confidence — 0 to 10 — 0 Cannot do it at all ↔ 10 Highly certain I can do it
07. 커피 한 잔인데, 세 잔이 주문됐네요?: 07. One coffee, but three drinks were ordered?
Choose one drink to order now.
Start by comparing input formats for selecting one category.
단일 선택 · 숫자는 범주 코드: Single choice · Numbers are category codes
목적에 맞는 선택: A choice that fits the purpose
Selecting one clears the previous selection. That matches a question asking for one drink.
Useful for a short list that is immediately visible.
복수 선택 · 중복 응답 가능: Multiple choices · More than one response allowed
현재 목적과 맞지 않음: Does not fit the current purpose
세 가지를 동시에 고를 수 있죠? 한 잔만 고르라는 질문과 설정이 충돌합: You can select all three at once. The setting conflicts with the instruction to choose one drink.
Use single choice, or change the question to “Select all drinks you would like.”
단일 선택 · 펼쳐서 고르기: Single choice · Open the list to select
It records the same categories as radio buttons, but respondents must open the list to see them.
Useful for a long list. Radio buttons also work for a short list.
차례로 살펴볼 힌트: Hints to consider one at a time
라디오·체크박스·드롭다운은 화면 형식입니다. 그 자체가 측정 수준은 아닙: Radio buttons, checkboxes, and dropdowns are interface formats. They do not by themselves define a level of measurement.
Americano = 1 and latte = 2 does not mean that a latte is twice an Americano.
First align the format with “choose one” or “select all that apply.”
08. ChatGPT도 쓰고, Gemini도 쓰는데요?: 08. What if I use both ChatGPT and Gemini?
Select all generative AI services you used in the past seven days.
사용한 서비스 목록 · 서비스별 사용 여부: Services used · Use or nonuse of each service
두 서비스를 쓴 사람도 하나만 남겨야 합니다. 사용한 서비스가 누락됩니다: Even someone who used two services must keep only one. Some use is lost.
Use checkboxes that allow all applicable services.
서비스마다 사용 여부를 따로 남길 수 있습니다. “사용 안 함”은 다른: Each service’s use can be recorded separately. “None used” cannot be selected with another option.
In a real survey, consider an Other option with a write-in field.
0 전혀 안 씀 ↔ 10 매우 많이 씀: 0 No use at all ↔ 10 Very heavy use
You can move a measure of amount, but it does not identify which services were used.
Ask about service type and amount of use in separate items.
“모두”라고 써 놓고 하나만 고르게 하지 않았나요?: Did you write “all” but allow only one selection?
A 0/1 code for each service indicates use or nonuse, not preference ranking.
Selecting several services together with “None used” creates a contradiction.
09. 아이폰과 갤럭시 사이 1.7은 뭔가요?: 09. What is 1.7 between an iPhone and a Galaxy?
현재 주로 쓰는 휴대폰 운영체제는 무엇입니까?: What operating system does the phone you mainly use have?
운영체제 한 범주 · A/B/C 입력 방식을 골라 직접 답하기: One operating-system category · Choose input format A/B/C and try answering
1.7이라는 응답은 어떤 운영체제일까요? 범주 코드 사이에 연속량을 만든: Which operating system is 1.7? This creates a continuous quantity between category codes.
Record different kinds as clearly defined categories.
X 1–9 / Y 1–9 · 두 축 의미 미정: X 1–9 / Y 1–9 · Neither axis has a defined meaning
점을 찍어도 두 축이 무엇인지 정의되지 않았습니다. 좌표가 질문에 답하지: You can place a point, but neither axis has been defined. The coordinates do not answer the question.
Do not use XY unless the purpose is to measure two dimensions.
iOS / Android / 기타 / 휴대폰 사용 안 함: iOS / Android / Other / I do not use a mobile phone
운영체제를 한 범주로 기록할 수 있습니다. 코드의 평균은 운영체제의 평균: This records an operating-system category. The mean of its codes is not an average operating system.
Define “mainly use” and include Other and nonuse categories.
응답 1.7을 연구자가 해석할 수 있나요?: Can the researcher interpret a response of 1.7?
Two coordinates do not automatically provide twice as much useful information.
이 목적에는 C가 적합합니다. 슬라이더 자체가 나쁜 도구라는 뜻은 아닙니: C fits this purpose. That does not mean sliders are inherently bad.
10. 지난 7일인데, 8일 썼다고요?: 10. Eight days of use in the past seven days?
지난 7일 강의 준비에 AI를 사용한 날은 며칠입니까?: On how many of the past seven days did you use AI to prepare for teaching?
사용 일수 · 0–7일 정수: Days of use · Integer from 0 to 7
A. 범위 제한 없는 숫자: A. Number without an upper limit
0 이상 일수 입력 · 상한 없음: Enter a nonnegative number of days · No upper limit
입력 범위: 0–상한 없음 / 간격 1 / 일: Input range: 0–No upper limit / Step 1 / Days
It accepts eight days. The allowed input range conflicts with the question’s time period.
Set a maximum of seven days and allow only integers.
The period and unit match. Zero days is a valid response.
Do not automatically save an untouched slider as zero days or a midpoint.
C. 0–7일 숫자 입력: C. Numeric input from 0 to 7 days
Typing a number can measure the same number of days.
Explain out-of-range values and decimals, then request a valid entry.
Number of uses and number of days used are different variables.
Without zero days, nonusers have no valid answer.
Both sliders and numeric input can work. Purpose, range, and unit are what matter.
11. 같은 7점인데, A와 C는 반대일까요?: 11. Both use seven points. Are A and C opposites?
중국 공산당에 대한 태도를 어떻게 물을까요?: How should we ask about attitudes toward the Chinese Communist Party?
A: “싫다”에 동의 / C: 호오를 직접 평가 · 가상 응답: A: agreement with “dislike” / C: direct liking–disliking rating · Fictional response
“나는 중국 공산당이 싫다.” · 1 전혀 동의 안 함 ↔ 7 매우 동의: “I dislike the Chinese Communist Party.” · 1 Strongly disagree ↔ 7 Strongly agree
1 전혀 아니다 / 2 아니다 / 3 약간 아니다 / 4 어느 쪽도 아니: 1 Strongly disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Somewhat disagree / 4 Neither / 5 Somewhat agree / 6 Agree / 7 Strongly agree
조건을 확인할 선택: A choice whose conditions need checking
A의 7점은 “싫다”는 문장에 매우 동의한다는 뜻입니다. 1점은 “싫다는: A score of 7 in A means strongly agreeing with “I dislike it.” A score of 1 means disagreeing with that statement, not necessarily liking it very much.
C도 7개 숫자지만 질문과 점수 방향이 다릅니다. A의 1점을 C의 7점: C also uses seven numbers, but the question and scoring direction differ. You cannot directly convert A’s 1 into C’s 7.
싫다 / 싫지 않다 · 두 범주: Dislike / Do not dislike · Two categories
고르기는 쉽지만 약간 싫음과 아주 싫음의 차이가 사라집니다. “싫지 않다: It is easy to choose, but the difference between slight and strong dislike disappears. Not disliking is not necessarily liking.
Decide whether you need only the direction of the attitude or its strength as well.
“중국 공산당을 얼마나 싫어하거나 좋아합니까?” · 1 매우 싫음 ↔ 7: “How much do you dislike or like the Chinese Communist Party?” · 1 Dislike very much ↔ 7 Like very much
1 매우 싫음 / 2 싫음 / 3 약간 싫음 / 4 좋지도 싫지도 않음: 1 Dislike very much / 2 Dislike / 3 Dislike somewhat / 4 Neither like nor dislike / 5 Like somewhat / 6 Like / 7 Like very much / Do not know / Prefer not to answer
C의 1점은 “매우 싫다”, 7점은 “매우 좋다”입니다. A와 대상은 같: In C, 1 means “dislike very much” and 7 means “like very much.” The target is the same as in A, but it asks directly about both poles instead of agreement with a negative statement.
C가 항상 정답은 아닙니다. 측정 목적에 맞는 표현을 고르고, 모름·응답: C is not always the correct choice. Match wording to the purpose, and separate not knowing or refusing from neutrality.
A’s 7 = strongly agreeing with “dislike.” C’s 7 = liking very much. The numbers match, but the directions are opposite.
A의 “싫지 않다”는 C의 “좋다”와 같을까요? 무관심이나 중립도 가능합: Is A’s “do not dislike” the same as C’s “like”? Indifference or neutrality is also possible. Reverse coding alone is not evidence of equivalence.
중간 응답자가 없다고 단정할 수 없습니다. 극단에 몰린다는 이유만으로 7: You cannot assume that nobody will choose the middle. Clustering at the extremes alone does not make seven points wrong or two points correct.
12. 4점: 중립? 모르겠음? 말하기 싫음?: 12. A score of 4: neutral, unsure, or unwilling to answer?
처음 듣는 “정책 Z”에 얼마나 동의합니까?: How much do you agree with “Policy Z,” which you have just heard about for the first time?
Answer as a fictional respondent who has no information about it.
모르는 사람에게도 숫자를 요구합니다. 4점에 모름이 섞이면 중립이라고 해: Even uninformed respondents must choose a number. If uncertainty is mixed into 4, that score is hard to interpret as neutral.
Provide distinct neutral and do-not-know categories.
1–7점 동의 + 잘 모름: Agreement from 1 to 7 + Do not know
1 전혀 동의 안 함 / 2 / 3 / 4 중립 / 5 / 6 / 7 매: 1 Strongly disagree / 2 / 3 / 4 Neutral / 5 / 6 / 7 Strongly agree / Do not know
잘 모름은 동의 정도 4점이나 0점이 아닙니다. 분석 때 별도 범주/결측: “Do not know” is neither agreement level 4 nor 0. Define a separate-category or missing-data rule for analysis.
Also consider whether a neutral description of the policy should be provided first.
1 강하게 반대 / 2 반대 / 3 찬성 / 4 강하게 찬성: 1 Strongly oppose / 2 Oppose / 3 Support / 4 Strongly support
중간을 없애면 의견이 생길까요? 정보 부족이 찬반 중 하나로 바뀌어 기록: Does removing the middle create an opinion? Lack of information is now recorded as support or opposition.
First justify whether forced support–opposition fits the research purpose.
중립은 태도의 위치이고, 모름은 판단할 정보가 부족한 상태일 수 있습니다: Neutrality is an attitudinal position; not knowing may mean insufficient information to judge.
Refusal and not applicable each have different meanings too.
중간값의 포함 여부에는 연구 목적과 응답자 검토가 필요합니다. 항상 넣거: Including a midpoint depends on the research purpose and respondent review. There is no rule to always include or always exclude it.
13. 성별 한 문항으로 두 정보를 알 수 있을까요?: 13. Can one sex/gender question give us two kinds of information?
출생 시 기록과 현재 성별 정체성 · 필요하면 별도 문항으로 측정: Sex recorded at birth and current gender identity · Measure separately when needed
질문이 현재 정체성인지 출생 시 기록인지 불명확하고, 두 범주로 자신을: It is unclear whether the question asks about current identity or the record at birth. People who do not describe themselves using those two categories may struggle to answer.
First define the concept needed, then review options for the target population.
“당신의 생물학적 성별은 무엇입니까?” · 남 / 여: “What is your biological sex?” · Male / Female
이 단어만으로 출생 시 기록인지, 어떤 신체적 특성인지 명확해지지는 않습: That word alone does not clarify whether you mean the record at birth or particular physical characteristics. It also does not establish current gender identity.
출생 시 기록이 필요한 연구라면 “출생 시 기록된 성별”처럼 그 변수를: If the study needs the record at birth, ask specifically about that variable, such as “sex recorded at birth.”
별도 문항: “현재 스스로 인식하는 성별은 무엇입니까?”: Separate item: “How do you currently describe your gender?”
남성 / 여성 / 논바이너리 / 다른 표현 사용 / 응답하고 싶지 않음: Man / Woman / Nonbinary / I use another term / Prefer not to answer
C는 B를 대체하는 만능 정답이 아닙니다. 출생 시 기록과 현재 정체성이: C is not a universal replacement for B. When research needs both the record at birth and current identity, add a separate item like C.
두 응답은 서로 다른 변수로 저장합니다. 목적에 필요 없는 정보까지 반드: Store the two answers as different variables. This does not mean collecting information that is unnecessary for the study.
B로 현재의 성별 정체성까지 알 수 있을까요? 서로 다른 정보를 한 문항: Can B also reveal current gender identity? One question cannot readily stand in for two different kinds of information.
연구에 둘 다 필요하면 ① 출생 시 기록된 성별 ② 현재 성별 정체성을: If both are needed, ask separately about (1) sex recorded at birth and (2) current gender identity. Simply choosing C does not complete the design.
성적 지향도 또 다른 변수입니다. 연구 목적에 필요한 정보만 수집하고 문: Sexual orientation is another distinct variable. Collect only what the study needs, and pretest wording and options with respondents.
14. 월 300만 원이면, 두 칸에 걸리는데요?: 14. A monthly income of KRW 3 million fits two boxes?
지난달 개인의 세전 소득은 얼마입니까?: What was your personal income before tax last month?
소득 구간을 구분하기 · 가상 인물: 월 300만 원: Distinguishing income bands · Fictional person: KRW 3 million per month
0–300만 원 / 300–500만 원 / 500만 원 이상: KRW 0–3 million / KRW 3–5 million / KRW 5 million or more
300만 원이 첫째와 둘째 구간에 모두 들어갑니다. 500만 원도 경계가: KRW 3 million fits both the first and second bands. The boundary also overlaps at KRW 5 million.
Clarify boundaries with “less than” on one side and “at least” on the other.
0 이상 300 미만 / 300 이상 500 미만 / 500 이상: 0 to under 300 / 300 to under 500 / 500 or more
0 이상 300만 원 미만 / 300 이상 500만 원 미만 / 500만: KRW 0 to under 3 million / KRW 3 million to under 5 million / KRW 5 million or more / Prefer not to answer
300만 원은 둘째 구간 하나에만 해당합니다. 이 예시는 음수가 아닌 소: KRW 3 million fits only the second band. This example assumes nonnegative income.
In actual research, also define how to handle losses, no income, uncertainty, and refusal.
만 원 단위 · 0 이상: Units of KRW 10,000 · Zero or more
입력 범위: 0–상한 없음 / 간격 1 / 만 원: Input range: 0–No upper limit / Step 1 / KRW 10,000
금액을 더 세밀하게 받을 수 있지만 기억 부담과 공개 부담이 커질 수 있: This allows greater precision but may increase recall and disclosure burdens.
Specify the necessary precision, definition of income, and refusal option.
Categories must not overlap, so one response cannot fit two boxes.
빠진 구간도 없어야 합니다. “기타”로 모든 설계 문제를 덮을 수는 없습: Do not leave gaps either. An Other option cannot solve every design problem.
개인/가구, 세전/세후, 월/연, 근로/전체 소득 중 무엇을 묻는지 적습: State whether you mean personal or household, before or after tax, monthly or annual, and earned or total income.
15. 이 문항, 어떻게 손보면 좋을까요?: 15. How should we repair this item?
I like generative AI and can use AI to draft teaching materials.
A. 이대로 사용한다: A. Use it as it is
“좋아한다에는 5점, 만들 수 있다에는 1점인데요?”: “I would give liking a 5, but being able to create a draft a 1.”
This tries to collect two judgments in one response.
Split liking and production confidence into separate items.
B. ‘나는 AI를 잘 쓴다’로 줄인다: B. Shorten it to “I am good at using AI”
“자주 쓴다는 뜻인가요? 결과물이 좋다는 뜻인가요?”: “Do you mean I use it often, or that I produce good results?”
It is shorter, but “good at” still means different things to different people.
Specify the task the respondent should be able to perform.
C. 호감과 제작 자신감을 나눈다: C. Separate liking from production confidence
“좋아하는 정도와 만들 자신감에 따로 답할게요.”: “I will answer separately about liking it and feeling able to create a draft.”
Separate responses let us distinguish the meaning of each score.
For example: (1) I enjoy using AI. (2) I can use AI to draft teaching materials. Answer each separately.
Change the basis for the five-point agreement response. The same 12 people remain.
가상 12명: 호감↑·자신감↓ 6명 / 호감↓·자신감↑ 3명 / 둘 다: Twelve fictional people: six with high liking and low confidence; three with low liking and high confidence; three moderate on both
수업용 가상 응답 — 실제 결과 예측이 아님. 같은 12명을 유지하며 응: Fictional classroom responses—not predictions of real results. We keep the same 12 people and change only the response rule. The compromise scenario assumes everyone chooses 3; it is not an arithmetic-mean rule. The point is that the score alone does not reveal which judgment was answered.
17. Split the question to reveal different judgments.
① AI를 활용하는 일이 좋다. ② AI로 강의자료 초안을 만들 수 있다: (1) I enjoy using AI. (2) I can use AI to draft teaching materials.
비교 실험에서는 두 문항 모두 1–5점 동의. 최종 자신감 문항은 0–1: Both items use agreement from 1 to 5 in this comparison. The final confidence items are designed separately on a 0–10 scale. The two scales are not converted.
18. 그래프만 보고 알 수 있는 것은?: 18. What can the graph alone tell us?
5점 동의 문항에서 3점(보통)에 응답이 몰렸습니다. 이유를 확정할 수: Responses cluster at 3, the midpoint of a five-point agreement item. Can we determine why?
That is one possible explanation, but it cannot be distinguished from compromising at the midpoint.
Examine both the item and respondents’ reasons for answering.
B. 이중질문이 틀림없다: B. It must be a double-barreled question
“다른 이유로도 가운데를 고를 수 있죠.”: “People can choose the middle for other reasons too.”
The shape of a distribution cannot by itself establish an item defect.
Check the meaning of the question and the response process.
C. 분포만으로 이유를 확정할 수 없다: C. The distribution alone cannot establish the reason
“어느 부분에 답했는지 다시 물어봐야겠어요.”: “We should ask which part they were answering.”
The same number can result from different judgments.
Ask, “How did you understand this question?”
19. 셋 다 좋은데, 꼭 꼴찌를 만들라고요?: 19. All three matter. Must one come last?
커피를 고를 때 가격·맛·접근성 중 무엇이 더 중요합니까?: When choosing coffee, which matters more: price, taste, or accessibility?
Compare each attribute’s importance with its relative priority.
1순위 가장 중요 → 3순위 덜 중요 · 동순위 없음: Rank 1 Most important → Rank 3 Less important · No ties
반드시 순서를 정하므로 상대적 우선순위를 알 수 있습니다. 1위가 2위보: A forced order reveals relative priority, but not how much more important first place is than second.
Decide whether ties are allowed and whether priority is actually what you need.
각 속성 1 전혀 중요 안 함 ↔ 5 매우 중요: Each attribute: 1 Not at all important ↔ 5 Very important
셋 다 5점이 가능합니다. 독립적 중요도를 묻기 때문에 반드시 차이가 나: All three can receive 5. Independent importance ratings need not differ.
우선순위가 목적이면 별도 순위를 묻습니다. 평정과 순위를 같은 값처럼 해: If priority is the goal, ask for ranking separately. Do not interpret ratings and ranks as the same values.
This identifies the top attribute but not the order of the remaining two.
Use ranking for the full order, or single choice if only the top option is needed.
Ranks 1, 2, and 3 establish order. Equal intervals are not guaranteed.
평정에서는 셋 다 중요할 수 있습니다. 그것만으로 잘못된 응답은 아닙니다: With ratings, all three can matter. That alone is not an invalid response.
Ranking and rating answer different questions.
20. 예산은 100인데, 합계가 180이네요?: 20. The budget is 100, but the total is 180?
Allocate 100 education-budget points among facilities, scholarships, and teaching support.
제한된 자원의 상대적 배분 · 총합 100: Relative allocation of limited resources · Total 100
한 항목에 더 주면 다른 항목에 줄 점수가 줄어듭니다. 제한된 자원 배분: Giving more to one item leaves fewer points for the others. This reveals allocation of limited resources.
합계 100을 확인하고 0점도 허용합니다. 이 점수는 독립적 만족도가 아: Check that the total is 100 and allow zero. These are not independent satisfaction ratings.
각 항목 독립 평정 · 합계 제한 없음: Independent ratings · No restriction on the total
All can receive high scores, but the 100-point budget constraint disappears.
Apply a total-sum constraint when asking about budget allocation.
Knowing that scholarships rank first does not tell us whether they receive 80 points or 34.
Use a constant-sum format if allocation shares are needed.
“How good is it?” differs from “How much of a limited budget would you give it?”
합계 제약 때문에 항목들이 서로 영향을 받습니다. 독립적 척도처럼 다루지: The total constraint makes responses interdependent. Do not treat them as independent scales.
합계 오류는 입력 검증 문제이고, 무엇을 배분시키는가는 측정 설계 문제입: An incorrect total is an input-validation problem; deciding what to allocate is a measurement-design problem.
21. 표로 만들면, 자동으로 같은 척도인가요?: 21. Does putting items in a table make them one scale?
강의실 평가: 깨끗하다 / 조용하다 / 찾아가기 쉽다: Classroom evaluation: clean / quiet / easy to find
각 속성에 대한 동의 · 같은 화면, 서로 다른 내용: Agreement with each attribute · One display, different content
각 행 1 전혀 동의 안 함 ↔ 5 매우 동의함: Each row: 1 Strongly disagree ↔ 5 Strongly agree
한 화면에서 세 판단을 따로 받습니다. 표에 함께 있다고 하나의 구성개념: One screen collects three separate judgments. Sharing a table does not automatically create one construct or justify an average score.
Check what each row asks and the grounds for combining them.
“깨끗하고 조용하고 찾기 쉽다” · 1–5점 동의: “Clean, quiet, and easy to find” · Agreement from 1 to 5
깨끗하지만 시끄러운 강의실에는 몇 점을 줘야 할까요? 세 판단이 한 점수: What score fits a classroom that is clean but noisy? Three judgments are combined into one score.
Separate judgments that respondents could answer differently.
그렇다고 여기는 속성은 알지만 동의 강도는 잃습니다. 체크하지 않은 이유: This identifies attributes considered present but loses degree of agreement. Reasons for leaving boxes unchecked may also be unclear.
정도까지 필요하면 행별 평정을, 존재 여부만 필요하면 명확한 이분형을 씁: Use row-by-row ratings for degree, or clear binary questions if only presence is needed.
A matrix is a display arrangement. It does not guarantee scale validity.
모든 행에 같은 열을 고르는 응답이 실제 생각인지 빠른 통과인지 확인이: Check whether choosing the same column in every row reflects real views or rapid completion.
큰 표는 읽기 부담이 큽니다. 모바일에서는 행을 나누는 방식도 검토합니다: Large tables create reading burden. Consider splitting rows on mobile screens.
22. AI 말투, 차가운가요 따뜻한가요?: 22. Does the AI’s tone feel cold or warm?
방금 본 AI 답변의 말투는 어떻게 느껴집니까?: How does the tone of the AI response you just saw feel?
The endpoints let respondents locate an impression on a single axis.
Check with respondents that the two adjectives actually form opposite ends for this target.
1–5개 · 별의 의미 설명 없음: 1–5 stars · No explanation of the stars’ meaning
Stars are familiar, but it is unclear whether they indicate coldness, warmth, or satisfaction.
Define the stars and endpoints, or present a semantic differential.
“이 AI 답변의 말투는 따뜻하다” · 1–5점 동의: “This AI response sounds warm” · Agreement from 1 to 5
1 전혀 동의 안 함 / 2 동의 안 함 / 3 보통 / 4 동의함 /: 1 Strongly disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Neither agree nor disagree / 4 Agree / 5 Strongly agree
따뜻하다는 문장에 동의하는 정도를 받습니다. 양극 형용사를 직접 비교하는: This measures agreement with a statement about warmth. Its wording differs from a direct comparison of bipolar adjectives.
The score range and wording differ, so do not directly pool values from different formats.
A familiar star shape does not automatically communicate its meaning.
“빠르다–정확하다”는 반대말 한 쌍이 아닙니다. 둘 다 높을 수 있습니다: “Fast–accurate” is not a pair of opposites. Both can be high.
의미분별과 동의 평정은 모두 가능하지만 같은 문항·같은 점수라고 가정하지: Both semantic differentials and agreement ratings can work, but do not assume they are the same item or score.
23. 배달 음식 별 1개: 맛이 없었나요, 늦었나요?: 23. One star for delivery: bad taste or late arrival?
이번 주문은 전반적으로 얼마나 만족스러웠습니까?: Overall, how satisfied were you with this order?
Distinguish overall satisfaction from reasons for dissatisfaction.
전반 만족은 빠르게 받을 수 있습니다. 별 1개만으로 맛과 배달 중 원인: This quickly records overall satisfaction. One star alone cannot identify whether taste or delivery caused dissatisfaction.
Use it for overall satisfaction, and add follow-up items to investigate reasons.
각 행 1 매우 불만족 ↔ 5 매우 만족: Each row: 1 Very dissatisfied ↔ 5 Very satisfied
Separate taste, delivery, and price ratings help identify the source of dissatisfaction.
Whether their simple average represents overall satisfaction requires separate examination.
0 전혀 추천 안 함 ↔ 10 매우 추천함: 0 Not at all likely to recommend ↔ 10 Extremely likely to recommend
만족과 추천 의향은 관련될 수 있지만 같은 질문이 아닙니다. 만족해도 가: Satisfaction and recommendation may be related, but they are different questions. Someone may be satisfied yet reluctant to recommend because of the price.
Distinguish overall satisfaction from recommendation according to the research purpose.
One number can provide an overall evaluation without revealing specific reasons.
Stars are a display format; satisfaction is the content being measured.
Overall and attribute ratings serve different roles.
24. 둘 다 9점인데, 같은 점수일까요?: 24. Both are 9. Are they the same score?
이 AI 도구를 동료에게 추천할 가능성은 얼마나 됩니까?: How likely are you to recommend this AI tool to a colleague?
추천 의향 · 숫자가 같아도 구성개념은 다를 수 있음: Likelihood to recommend · Identical numbers can represent different constructs
9점은 높은 추천 의향입니다. NPS 방식에서는 9–10점을 추천 고객: A 9 indicates a high likelihood of recommending. In the NPS system, responses of 9–10 are classified as promoters.
NPS는 추천 고객 비율에서 비추천 고객 비율을 뺀 집계값입니다. 개인의: NPS is an aggregate: the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors. An individual’s score of 9 is not itself NPS.
0 전혀 만들 수 없음 ↔ 10 확실히 만들 수 있음: 0 Cannot create it at all ↔ 10 Highly certain I can create it
9점이 나와도 이는 제작 자신감입니다. 추천 의향이라는 질문과 눈금이 어: A 9 here represents production confidence. The scale does not match a question about recommendation.
Align the anchors with likelihood of recommending.
A satisfaction scale does not directly answer a question about recommendation likelihood.
Do not substitute recommendation, satisfaction, and confidence just because each produces a number.
0–10 is a numerical range, not a construct.

교수님, 저 주제를 아직 잡고 있어요: Professor, I am still working on my topic
안창현 · 한림대학교 미디어스쿨 · 2026년 10월 20일: Changhyun Ahn · Hallym University Media School · October 20, 2026
지난주 수업 경험에서 출발합니다. 민서와 면담·과제 상황은 가상 사례이며: We begin with the instructor’s classroom experience. Minseo, her meetings, and assignment situations are fictional examples. Actual research is identified with its sources.
지난주, 7점 중 2점: Last week: two out of seven
지난주 2점과 몇 개월째인 주제: Last week’s confidence and the months spent on a topic
지난주에 제가 여러분께 물었습니다. 설문조사 문항을 직접 만들 자신이 얼: Last week I asked how confident you felt about writing survey questions yourselves. On a seven-point scale, what would you choose? As I remember it, more than ninety percent of roughly ten students answered two.
여러분이 AI를 못 쓰는 사람들도 아닙니다. GPT도 쓰고 클로드도 쓰고: You are hardly strangers to AI. You use GPT and Claude, upload papers for summaries, and generate the writing you need. About half of you also completed a whole methods course last semester. Yet when I ask whether you could write a few survey items with your own hands, you are not confident.
그 2점을 그냥 넘길 수 없었습니다: We cannot simply move past that two
저는 그 대답을 듣고 수업을 어떻게 해야 하나 다시 고민했습니다. “자신: That answer made me rethink this course. I could not simply say, ‘Have confidence,’ and move on. Nor does choosing two prove that your actual ability is two out of seven. We just learned to distinguish confidence from performance. But we do need to examine what you rely on when starting research, and where you stop.
There is something I keep hearing.
“교수님, 저 아직 주제를 잡고 있어요.”: ‘Professor, I am still working on my topic.’
주제가 맨손으로 잡는 멧돼지입니까: Is your topic a wild boar to catch?
처음 들으면 그럴 수 있습니다. 관심 있는 분야를 둘러보고 있을 수도 있: The first time, that is understandable. Perhaps you are exploring a field, or reading has changed your mind. But a month later, the answer is the same. Next semester, much the same. You reach your second or third semester and you are still trying to catch a topic. Is this topic a wild boar you have to catch with your bare hands? You keep hunting it, but we never get to see its face.
주제가 맨손으로 잡는 멧돼지입니까 · 이어서: Is your topic a wild boar to catch? — continued
그동안 아무것도 안 했느냐고 물으면 그것도 아닙니다. 자료를 찾았고, A: It is not as if you did nothing. You found materials, asked AI, and wrote down possible titles. But when I ask, ‘What have you learned since last time?’ the answer becomes vague again.
그 ‘조금 더’는 언제 끝납니까: When does a little more end?
“조금 더 정리해서 말씀드리려고요.”: ‘I wanted to organize things a little more before telling you.’
바로 그 ‘조금 더’가 오늘 우리가 붙잡을 부분입니다. 얼마나 더 준비해: That ‘a little more’ is what we need to examine. How much more must you prepare before you can come? Who decides when you are ready? If you keep preparing because you cannot make that judgment alone, will spending longer in the same place resolve it?
오늘 바꿀 것은 제목보다 질문입니다: Change the question before the title
오늘은 완성된 논문 제목을 하나씩 들고 나가라고 하지 않겠습니다. 대신: Today I will not ask everyone to leave with a finished thesis title. Instead, let us record what you have checked, what you do not know, and whose help you need with which question. If the class ends and you return to ‘I understood, but my own research is still…,’ entertaining explanations alone will not have finished our work.
주제를 아직 정하지 못한 학생을 하나 놓고 생각해봅시다. 이름은 민서라고: Let us follow a student who has not settled on a topic. We will call her Minseo. She is a fictional master's student, rather than an account of any particular person.
민서는 AI와 미디어에 관심이 있습니다. 딥페이크도 문제 같고, 가짜뉴스: Minseo is interested in AI and media. Deepfakes seem concerning, misinformation seems concerning, and she wonders why people trust AI-generated content. She has plenty of interests. Turning an interest into a research topic is where she gets stuck.
지도교수님을 찾아가야 한다는 건 알고 있습니다. 그런데 빈손으로 가기에는: She knows she should visit her advisor, but feels bad about arriving empty-handed. She cannot confidently answer, ‘What do you want to do?’ Perhaps she should read some papers first. She does not know how many would be enough. She starts searching.
논문 대신 탭이 스무 개가 됐습니다: Twenty tabs instead of a paper read
검색 결과가 많습니다. 너무 많습니다. 제목을 보면 다 내 주제와 관계가: There are many results. Far too many. From their titles, every paper seems relevant; from their abstracts, perhaps none is. Unfamiliar theories appear, and the analysis methods are even less familiar. She opens another paper, follows its references, and soon has twenty browser tabs.
At this point she wants to ask GPT.
“AI와 가짜뉴스에 관한 석사논문 주제 추천해줘.”: ‘Recommend master's thesis topics about AI and misinformation.’
단어가 줄을 서니 진도가 난 것 같습니다: A line of terms feels like progress
답이 나옵니다. 아주 그럴듯합니다. 신뢰, 리터러시, 수용 의도, 사회적: The answer looks excellent. Trust, literacy, acceptance intention, social influence, moderation: the terms line up. Alone, she could not produce one sentence. Now she has to scroll. It feels like progress.
그런데 민서는 여전히 어느 주제가 가능한지 모릅니다. 어떤 연구가 이미: Yet Minseo still cannot tell which topic is feasible or what research already exists. Since she cannot judge which terms to remove, perhaps she needs them all. She asks AI for more detail. A rationale appears, then theoretical background, then hypotheses.
교수님께 보여드릴 파일은 점점 길어집니다. 설명할 자신은 이상하게 더 줄: The file she can show her professor grows longer. Strangely, her confidence in explaining it keeps shrinking.
I understand why you use AI in this situation. Time is short. A deadline is approaching, you said the work was underway, and you need something to show. ‘Read enough and think carefully’ can be infuriating advice when no one can tell you when enough ends.
그래서 오늘은 AI를 쓰기 직전으로 시간을 되돌려서, 의지만 강해지면 해: So we will not rewind to before AI and claim that stronger willpower would solve everything. Minseo continues using AI. She chooses which of its contributions she needs now, and reduces what she must check to a manageable size.
교수자도 해야 할 일이 있습니다: The teacher has work to do too
교수자도 할 일이 있습니다. 처음 연구하는 학생에게 “좀 더 고민해보세요: The teacher has work to do too. If a beginner hears only ‘Think about it more,’ they cannot tell whether that means searching, reading, or changing topics. I can write quickly in my own field because I can judge which explanations are missing, which studies connect, and what need not be written yet. If I demand the same AI-assisted speed from a beginner, the easiest thing for the student to imitate is the page count.
그러니 제 쪽에서도 말을 바꿔야겠습니다. “더 생각해오세요”로 끝내지 않: I must change my instructions as well. Instead of ending with ‘Think more,’ I should specify which material to check, and how far, before our next conversation. You must also show where you stopped. If we wait without seeing either side, next week's meeting will repeat the same exchange.
“서울에 갈게요.” 서울 어디요?: I am going to Seoul. Where in Seoul?
“저는 AI와 가짜뉴스를 연구하고 싶습니다.”: ‘I want to research AI and misinformation.’
좋습니다. 관심 있는 동네는 정했습니다. 그런데 아직 어디로 갈지 정한: Good: we have identified a neighborhood of interest, but not a destination. It is like saying, ‘I want to go to Seoul,’ and asking which subway to take. Where in Seoul? To a hospital, a concert, or a friend's home?
여기서 “연구문제를 구체화하세요”라고 하면 또 어렵습니다. 민서에게는 이: ‘Make your research question more specific’ may still sound difficult. I will ask Minseo this instead.
Imagine that she thinks for a moment and answers.
“같은 뉴스라도 AI가 썼다고 하면 사람들이 덜 믿을 것 같아요.”: ‘I think people might trust the same news less if they are told AI wrote it.’
이 정도면 대화를 시작할 수 있습니다. 원래 문장에는 AI와 가짜뉴스라는: Now we can begin a conversation. Her first sentence contained two enormous terms, AI and misinformation. This one contains someone seeing something and responding: reading news, encountering information about AI authorship, and perhaps trusting it less.
벌써 학술적으로 바꾸지 마세요: Do not rush into academic language
이 말을 곧바로 학술적인 문장으로 바꾸지는 마세요. “생성형 인공지능 기: Do not rush to turn this into academic prose. Once ‘the disclosure of the production agency of generative-AI-based news content…’ starts expanding, Minseo loses her own words again. Hold on to ‘Would people trust it less if it said AI wrote it?’ for now.
“AI가 썼으면 그 뉴스는 가짜뉴스예요?”: ‘If AI wrote it, does that make it misinformation?’
AI가 쓰면 가짜뉴스입니까: Does AI authorship mean false news?
아니죠. 사실을 담은 뉴스도 AI가 정리할 수 있습니다. 사람이 썼어도: No. AI can organize factual news, and a human can write something false. Minseo started with ‘AI and misinformation,’ but her present question concerns how people interpret an authorship label, rather than whether the news itself is true.
단어 하나를 잠깐 내려놓은 것뿐인데 검색할 방향이 달라집니다. ‘가짜뉴스: Putting one term aside changes the search direction. Someone who kept searching for misinformation can now look for AI authorship labels, news judgments, AI-generated labels, and news accuracy.
내 말을 검색어로 바꿉니다: Turn your words into search terms
여기서 AI를 쓰면 됩니다. 어려운 연구 제목을 더 많이 뽑아달라고 하기: This is a useful place for AI. Rather than requesting more impressive research titles, ask it to turn your words into search terms.
“내가 궁금한 것은 같은 뉴스라도 AI가 썼다고 표시하면 사람들이 덜 믿: ‘I wonder whether people trust identical news less when it is labeled as written by AI. Suggest Korean and English search terms for relevant papers. Distinguish actual AI authorship from labeling something as AI-written. For now, give me search expressions rather than inventing paper titles or references.’
이 요청을 외울 필요는 없습니다. 여러분이 해야 할 말은 “내가 궁금한: You need not memorize that prompt. The essential request is: ‘This is the situation I am curious about. What terms would researchers use to find it?’
찾지 못한 논문은 읽은 논문이 아닙니다: An unfound paper is not a paper read
검색어를 얻었으면 실제 검색 결과를 열어봅니다. AI가 논문을 추천했다면: Open real search results after getting the terms. If AI recommends a paper, verify that its title and authors actually exist. If the link leads elsewhere or you cannot find the original, record that status. Just do not put an unfound paper on your list of papers read.
Even here, you can stop and ask a teacher.
“저는 AI가 작성했다는 표시가 뉴스 판단에 주는 영향이 궁금합니다. 이: ‘I am interested in how an AI authorship label affects news judgments. I searched with these terms, but I am unsure whether this is the field I should enter.’
열 편을 읽기 전에도 물을 수 있습니다: You can ask before reading ten papers
아직 논문 열 편을 읽지 않았습니다. 그래도 ‘주제를 잡고 있어요’보다: You have not read ten papers yet. Still, this makes the place where you need help much more visible than ‘I am working on my topic.’
실제 논문에서 무엇을 읽는가: What to read in an actual paper
실제 논문을 한 편 열어봅시다. Altay와 Gilardi가 2024년에: Let us open an actual paper by Altay and Gilardi, published in 2024. Even the first part of its long title could alarm Minseo: people are more skeptical of headlines labeled as AI-generated. The study reports two online experiments in the United States and United Kingdom. Original paper: Altay & Gilardi, 2024.
“교수님, 제가 하려던 거 이미 했는데요.”: ‘Professor, they already did what I wanted to do.’
읽기 전에 버리거나 새롭다고 하지 마세요: Do not discard or declare novelty yet
그 말이 나왔으면 지금 검색은 일을 한 겁니다. 여러분 생각이 형편없다는: If you can say that, searching has done its job. It has not delivered a verdict that your thinking is worthless. You can now examine how someone approached a similar question.
그런데 이때 두 가지로 급하게 뛰지 마세요. 하나는 “이미 했으니까 버릴: Do not rush to either of two conclusions: ‘They did it, so I will abandon it,’ or ‘Then I will just use Korean undergraduates.’ You do not yet have enough material for either judgment. You would be discarding it, or declaring novelty, before reading.
먼저, 어디가 겹치는지 봅니다: First find where the overlap is
오늘 이 논문에서 처음 확인할 것은 세상의 모든 선행연구가 아닙니다. 지: We are not beginning with every paper in the world. First find out how far this particular study actually overlaps your question.
논문을 열어 초록을 읽고, 연구 1의 ‘Design and procedu: Open the paper, read the abstract, and find Study 1's ‘Design and procedure.’
In the PDF we obtained, it is on page 3.
무엇을 보여주고 무엇을 물었습니까: What did they show and ask?
It explains what participants saw and what they answered.
연구자들은 뉴스 제목들을 제시하고, 제목의 주장이 얼마나 정확한지 또는: The researchers presented news headlines and asked how accurate their claims were, or how willing participants were to share them.
연구 1에서는 참가자 절반이 정확성을, 나머지 절반이 공유 의향을 평가했: In Study 1, half the participants evaluated accuracy, and the other half evaluated willingness to share.
Both responses used a scale from one to six.
정확성의 양끝은 ‘분명히 거짓’과 ‘분명히 참’에 해당하고, 공유 의향은: The accuracy endpoints correspond to definitely false and definitely true; the sharing endpoints correspond to very unlikely and very likely.
원문, 연구 1의 Design and procedure: Original paper, Study 1: Design and procedure.
정확하면 전부 공유합니까: Do you share everything you believe?
잠깐 멈춰봅시다. 우리가 처음 쓴 말은 “덜 믿는다”였습니다. 그런데 논: Pause. Our initial phrase was ‘trust less.’ The paper distinguishes judging something accurate from wanting to share it.
