이런 다른 이야기를 구별하려고 연구 방법을 고민합니다. 먼저 일어난 일을: Research methods help distinguish these alternative accounts. We examine what happened first, construct comparisons, and decide how to handle other conditions. Memorizing ‘correlation is not causation’ and then attaching ‘affects’ to every hypothesis does not help the manuscript.
뉴스 내용과 표시를 함께 바꾸면?: Changing the news and the label together?
민서의 뉴스 표시 연구로 돌아가봅시다. 서로 다른 사람에게 서로 다른 뉴: Return to Minseo's label study. If different people see entirely different news and give different ratings, the label and the news content are confounded. For our classroom example, we can imagine identical content with different labels. We can also consider assigning participants randomly rather than letting them choose which condition to see.
무작위 배정 한마디로 끝나지 않습니다: Random assignment is not the whole design
이렇게 하면 어떤 차이를 더 잘 따져볼 수 있는지 이해가 되죠. 그렇다고: That makes the comparison easier to understand. But writing ‘random assignment’ does not prepare an actual study. Check whether participants noticed the label, interpreted it as intended, and saw suitable news items, and whether the required participants are accessible. Obtain guidance and complete applicable ethics procedures before collecting data from people. Do not immediately distribute a survey link based on this exercise.
방법이 막힌 자리도 면담 질문입니다: A methods blockage is a meeting question
여기서 면담할 이유가 하나 더 생깁니다. “제가 하려는 질문은 한 번 설: Here is another reason for a meeting: ‘I cannot judge whether a one-time survey can answer my question, or whether I need a comparison using different labels.’ That is a question developed by studying methods. Revealing what you do not know is not a reason to hide again.
AI를 쓰지 말라는 말이 아닙니다: This is not a ban on AI
AI에게 맡길 일의 크기: The size of the task I give AI
저는 AI를 쓰지 말라고 이 수업을 하는 게 아닙니다. 옵시디언과 코덱스: I am not teaching this class to tell you to stop using AI. Teaching Obsidian and Codex while quietly insisting ‘just do everything yourself’ would understandably confuse you. AI can do substantial work. Adjust the size of what you delegate to the range you can currently judge.
전문가는 안 치는 동안에도 판단합니다: Experts judge even when they barely type
Imagine an expert quickly drafting with AI. While reading, they can recognize weak evidence, an already studied idea, a theory that complicates the explanation, or a comparison their data cannot support. On screen they may type little, but their judgment remains active.
초심자는 그 판단까지 통째로 AI에게 물어볼 수 있습니다. “이거 맞아?: A beginner may delegate that judgment as well. ‘Is this right?’ One AI says yes, and a second AI agrees. Agreement between two models does not verify the original source or establish feasibility. They may have produced the same plausible account.
그래서 오늘은 AI가 맡을 수 있는 일을 작게 잘라봅시다. 내 관심을 검: Cut AI's assignments into smaller tasks: converting an interest into search terms, locating a passage, explaining difficult sentences, or finding inconsistent uses of a term in two sentences you wrote. These can help because their results are small enough to compare with actual material.
한 번에 맡긴 판단이 너무 많습니다: Too many judgments delegated at once
반대로 “내 분야에서 독창적이고 실행 가능하며 지도교수님이 좋아할 주제를: In contrast, ‘Choose an original, feasible thesis topic my advisor will like and write the proposal’ bundles many judgments you cannot yet check. That is why even diligent rereading of the output may leave you unsure where verification should begin.
실제 연구가 본 것은 무엇입니까: What did the actual study examine?
실제 연구에서도 이 문제를 살펴보고 있습니다. Lee 등의 2025년 연: Researchers are examining this problem too. Lee and colleagues' 2025 study analyzed a survey of 319 generative-AI-using knowledge workers and examples of their work. It examined relationships among confidence in AI, confidence in one's own task performance, and self-reported critical evaluation, including difficulties under time pressure and in unfamiliar domains. It is a self-report survey, not an experiment proving that AI reduces graduate students' intelligence. Lee et al., 2025, CHI.
“검수하세요” 다음을 가르쳐야 합니다: Teach what comes after Verify it
이 논문을 우리 수업에 가져오는 이유도 “그러니까 AI를 멀리하라”는 결: We bring it into class to remember that checking outputs requires background knowledge and time, rather than to conclude that you should avoid AI. If we tell students only ‘Always verify AI drafts,’ they may have to ask AI how to verify them. That is why we are dividing the task into specific locations and questions.
그런데 다음 주까지 15페이지랍니다: But fifteen pages are due next week
민서에게 급한 일이 생겼다고 합시다. 다음 주까지 프로포절 15페이지를: Suppose Minseo is suddenly told to bring a fifteen-page proposal next week. A moment ago she thought, ‘Now I know what to do.’ Now her hand reaches for GPT again.
그 마음을 이해합니다. 여기서 “진짜 공부에는 지름길이 없습니다”라고 말: I understand. Saying ‘There are no shortcuts to real learning’ will not move the deadline. But abandoning today's approach, generating fifteen pages, and revising all weekend can leave her entering another meeting unable to explain her own writing.
우선 제출 조건부터 확인해야 합니다. 15페이지 안에 반드시 들어가야 하: First check the assignment. Which sections are required? Do references count toward fifteen pages? Is an exploratory plan acceptable, and what feedback is the assignment intended to obtain? If these instructions already exist, retrieve them rather than asking again. Follow any prescribed format.
초안 앞에 확인한 문장을 놓습니다: Put verified sentences before the draft
그다음 원고 전체를 처음부터 생성하기 전에, 오늘 확인한 문장을 앞에 놓: Before generating the whole manuscript, place today's verified sentences in front of you: what you want to know, which study you actually checked, what overlaps it, and what remains undecided. This is not an exemption from fifteen pages. It is an anchor that keeps those pages from making incompatible claims.
Give AI both that anchor and the assignment requirements.
AI에게 줄 기준도 구체적으로 씁니다: Give AI a concrete basis for drafting
“아래는 내가 원문에서 확인한 내용과 아직 결정하지 못한 내용이야. 교수: ‘Below is what I checked in the original and what remains undecided. First suggest where these belong within the required outline. Mark missing evidence rather than filling gaps with plausible prose. Do not invent references. Let us draft the parts supported by what I checked first.’
“아직 모름”이 확신으로 바뀝니다: I do not know becomes certainty
이렇게 해도 출력은 확인해야 합니다. AI는 ‘아직 모름’이라고 적은 내: Even then, check the output. AI can smooth ‘I do not know yet’ into a confident assertion. Review one paragraph before requesting the entire draft. Confirm that it contains your question and verified evidence, then proceed.
첫 문단에 온 세상을 집어넣지 마세요: Do not put the whole world in paragraph one
가령 연구의 필요성에 “AI 뉴스의 급증으로 전 세계 시민의 정보 판별: Suppose its rationale begins, ‘The rapid rise of AI news is sharply reducing citizens' information-discrimination abilities worldwide.’ Where did you verify that? The paper Minseo read does not establish that enormous claim. Before polishing it, reduce it to what the evidence can actually support.
“AI가 생성했다는 표시는 콘텐츠를 판단할 때 하나의 단서가 될 수 있다: ‘An AI-generated label can be a cue in evaluating content. It is useful to examine how people interpret that label.’
작게 써도 근거가 있으면 시작입니다: Small, supported sentences can start a draft
이 정도 문장부터 시작할 수 있습니다. 그다음에는 관련 논문을 확인해 어: You can start with a sentence of that size, then use relevant papers to state what was observed in which circumstances. Do not place an unread account of the entire world in the opening paragraph because you think academic writing must begin grandly.
작업용 초안에는 미확인 표시를 남겨도 됩니다. 다만 제출 전에는 그 표시: A working draft may contain unverified markers. Before submission, do not solve them by deleting the markers and pretending certainty. Verify and retain supportable claims, explain decisions that remain open in the research plan, or discuss what you can submit by the deadline. A shortage of pages does not justify inventing citations or confidence.
전문가를 일주일에 따라잡지는 못해도: Even if you cannot become an expert in a week
일주일 안에 전문가의 지식을 따라잡을 수 있다고 약속하지 않겠습니다. 지: I cannot promise that you will acquire an expert's knowledge in one week, or that an advisor will welcome every uncertainty. Still, entering a meeting knowing where the unfinished parts are differs from bringing a complete-looking manuscript that you can scarcely explain.
“이걸 질문이라고 가져왔어요?”: You brought this as a question?
그럴까 봐 못 가는 거죠. 저는 “막히면 바로 오세요. 안 혼내니까 물어: ‘What if my professor says, You brought this as a question?’ That fear is precisely why you hesitate. I invite you to come when stuck and say I will not scold you, but research groups differ. A supervisor's words can greatly affect a student's next action. Dismissing that concern as unnecessary worry will not produce a workable route to the meeting.
상처 견디기가 연구 훈련은 아닙니다: Enduring humiliation is not research training
Nor do I want to call enduring humiliation research training. Students have a responsibility to prepare questions, and teachers have a responsibility to make the next action understandable. Graduate advising guidance also describes supervision as a shared responsibility, with mutual expectations about meetings and drafts. Cornell Graduate School, Advising Guide for Research Students, 2025.
지금 민서가 할 수 있는 일은 질문을 조금 더 답하기 쉬운 형태로 만드는: Minseo can make the question easier to answer.
교수자가 고쳐줄 대상을 보여줍니다: Give the teacher something to correct
“교수님, 주제 뭐 할까요?”라고만 하면 교수님은 민서가 어디까지 와 있: ‘Professor, what should my topic be?’ does not show how far she has come. Try this instead.
“AI가 작성했다는 표시가 뉴스의 정확성 판단에 미치는 영향이 궁금해서: ‘I searched because I wondered how an AI authorship label affects accuracy judgments. I checked one paper's methods and found that a condition I thought was new was already there. I cannot judge whether to keep exploring this interest. Could you point me toward the paper or distinction I should examine next?’
“더 읽어보세요”를 들었다면: If the answer is Read more
이 질문을 했다고 칭찬을 보장받는 것은 아닙니다. 그래도 교수자가 고쳐줄: This does not guarantee praise, but it gives the teacher something to correct. If they say not to judge from one paper, ask what range to examine. If the measured concept is unclear, ask which concepts need separating.
“논문을 더 읽어보세요”라는 답을 들었다면, 그 자리에서 한 번 더 물어: If the answer is ‘Read more papers,’ ask once more while you are there.
“제가 다음에 읽을 때, AI 표시의 종류를 비교하는 데 집중하면 될까요: ‘In my next reading, should I focus on types of AI labels, or should I first examine the difference between accuracy judgments and trust?’
방향 없이 검색창으로 돌아오지 않게: Do not return to the search box without direction
이것도 선택지가 잘못됐다면 교수님이 고쳐주실 수 있습니다. 아무 방향 없: The professor can correct those options too. Leaving with an undirected instruction to read more may put you back at the search box next week.
면담이 어려우면 연락 방식부터: If meetings are difficult, clarify contact
면담을 잡기 어려우면 교수자가 허용하는 연락 방식과 질문 범위를 확인해두: If meetings are difficult to arrange, clarify the professor's preferred contact method and scope of questions. Can you send a short update, collect questions for a fixed time, or show a section before the whole draft? While waiting, continue feasible reading and recording. One delayed reply need not stop every exploration. A course teacher or senior student may help with reading practices, while final topic and direction still need confirmation within the advising relationship.
한 문단을 못 읽은 상태도 가져오세요: Bring the paragraph you could not understand
면담 한 장을 준비하려고 또 일주일을 혼자 버티지는 마세요. 논문을 못: Do not spend another week struggling alone to prepare a perfect meeting sheet. Bring the unsuccessful search if you could not find a paper; bring the paragraph you could not understand. You can show me that state too. We need to see the blockage to choose the next action together.
면담 후 “혼났다”만 남았습니까: Did the meeting leave only I got scolded?
면담을 다음 작업으로 바꾸기: Turning a meeting into the next task
민서가 면담을 다녀왔다고 합시다. “주제가 너무 넓다”, “그건 이미 연: Suppose Minseo returns from a meeting after hearing, ‘The topic is too broad,’ ‘That has already been studied,’ ‘Distinguish your concepts,’ and ‘Read this paper.’ She may feel bad. But if her only note is ‘Start over,’ what will she do tomorrow?
GPT에게 다시 주제 열 개를 추천받을 수도 있습니다. 그러면 오늘 확인: She may ask GPT for ten new topics. Then today's discoveries disappear from the next task.
교수님의 말과 내 해석을 나눕니다: Separate the advice from your interpretation
면담이 끝나면 교수님의 말과 내가 해석한 것을 나눠 적어보세요. 예를 들: Separate what the professor said from your interpretation. If the feedback was ‘Distinguish accuracy judgments and trust,’ record those words. Then write, ‘I understood this as a request to compare their measurement items.’ Do not assume the two statements are identical.
교수님의 말과 내 해석을 나눕니다 · 이어서: Separate the advice from your interpretation — continued
이해가 애매하면 확인할 수 있습니다. “오늘 말씀을 제가 이렇게 이해했습: If unclear, confirm: ‘This is how I understood today's advice. Should I next compare how the two concepts were measured?’ Use the teacher's preferred method for a brief check.
“논문 공부하기”보다 끝이 보이는 일: A task with an observable finish
그리고 다음 작업을 작게 적습니다. “논문 공부하기”라고 쓰지 말고 “추: Write a small next task. Instead of ‘Study papers,’ try ‘Find how the recommended paper measured trust, and place its items beside the accuracy items in the paper I already read.’ You will be able to tell when you have done it.
옵시디언의 기존 노트에도 한 줄을 보탭니다. 처음 질문을 지워버리지는 마: Add a line to the existing Obsidian note without erasing the first question: ‘Initially I grouped everything as trusting less. After the meeting, I will distinguish accuracy judgments from trust.’ Next week's you can then see why the question changed.
다음 대화가 지난 작업을 알 수 있게: Let the next conversation know the last task
AI에게도 이 기록을 주면 됩니다. “지난번에 정한 방향은 이거야. 오늘: Give that record to AI too: ‘This is the direction we chose last time. Today help with this comparison.’ That can reduce the habit of beginning every new chat with ‘Recommend a good master's thesis topic.’
여러분이 아무것도 모르던 사람이 아니라, 어디까지 확인한 사람인지 다음: Make it possible for the next task to recognize how far you have checked, rather than treating you as someone who knows nothing. Those accumulated links let your readings connect.
이해한 다음, 내 문장은 어디에 있습니까: After understanding, where is your own sentence?
수업 뒤 이어갈 내 문장: My sentence for continuing after class
여기까지 읽고 “쉽게 이해됐습니다”라고 하면 저는 반갑습니다. 하지만 오: I am glad if you found the explanation easy to understand. But let us carry it beyond that reaction. Consider the sentence you use for your own interest. It need not concern AI or misinformation: fandom, short videos, health information, games, political communication, or something else is fine.
‘영향’을 사람의 행동으로 풀어봅니다: Turn effects into people and actions
If it ends in ‘an effect on,’ describe the people and actions on each side. Who sees what, and what might they do differently? If you cannot answer, record that. Even knowing that ‘fandom's effect on consumption’ leaves you unable to distinguish purchasing from recommending provides a point to ask about.
자료 하나에서 내 질문이 움직이는지: Can one source change your question?
AI를 이용해 검색어를 만들고 실제 자료를 하나 열어봅니다. 한 편을 찾: Use AI to develop search terms and open one real source. Finding one paper does not finalize a topic. Check where it overlaps your question. Locate one part of the methods describing what people actually did. See whether reading it changes how you express your interest.
도저히 찾지 못하면 제게 그 화면을 보여주세요. “아직 준비가 안 됐는데: If you cannot find it, show me the screen. Do not close it with ‘I am not ready yet.’ We can examine whether the terms are too broad, whether another field uses different language, or whether you found the paper but not the relevant passage.
미확인은 낙인이 아니라 작업 상태입니다: Unverified is a work status, not a stigma
자료를 찾은 분은 출처와 직접 확인한 위치를 남겨주세요. AI가 해석한: If you found material, record the source and exact location you checked. Mark AI-only interpretations as unverified. That is today's work status, not a lifelong label of failure. It can change after you check tomorrow.
그리고 질문을 하나 씁니다. 교수님이 내 노트를 보고 무엇을 도와주셨으면: Write one question: what would you like your professor to help you judge? If you want to ask ‘Did I do well?’ divide it further. Is the question too broad? Have you distinguished two concepts? Is the study feasible with the time and material available?
어디를 읽고 어떤 말이 바뀌었습니까: Where did you read, and what changed?
저는 여러분이 고른 제목의 멋부터 보지 않겠습니다. 어디를 읽었는지, 그: I will look beyond an impressive title to where you read, which words changed after reading, and what you plan to check next. If explanation breaks down, we can stop there together. Do not pass that moment by reciting AI's long sentence. Help can reach the right place when we can see what you do not know.
어디를 읽고 어떤 말이 바뀌었습니까 · 이어서: Where did you read, and what changed? — continued
Begin with one sentence at the bottom of your note.
**“교수님, 제가 여기까지 확인했는데, 이 부분을 혼자 판단하기 어렵습: **‘Professor, this is what I have checked so far, and this is the part I cannot judge alone.’**
“교수님, 제가 여기까지 확인했는데, 이 부분을 혼자 판단하기 어렵습니다: ‘Professor, this is what I have checked so far, and this is the part I cannot judge alone.’
‘여기’에는 링크, ‘이 부분’에는 질문: A link for Here and a question for This part
‘여기’에 링크를 붙이세요. ‘이 부분’에 실제 질문을 쓰세요. 다 못: Attach a link to ‘this is what I checked.’ Put a real question in ‘this part.’ If you cannot fill everything in, show the places that are still empty.
오늘 따라온 과정을 자기 관심 문장이나 막힌 원고에서 이어갑니다. 스킬: Continue the process with your own interest or a draft where you are stuck. Download the skill ZIP and the empty student Obsidian vault, then follow the getting-started guide.
Advisor는 실제 논문을 찾아 읽을 범위를 좁히고, 본인이 설명한 것: The Advisor finds actual papers, narrows what to read, and records what you explained and what remains unknown. It does not count AI’s explanations as knowledge the student already possesses.
이 문장으로 시작하면 됩니다: You can begin with this sentence
완성된 프로포절을 준비한 뒤에 시작할 필요는 없습니다. 첫 관심 문장,: You do not need a finished proposal to begin. Bring an initial interest, a passage where reading stopped, or feedback from your advisor.
그 말을 지금 몇 개월째 하고 계십니까? 안창현 · 한림대학교 미디어스쿨:
How many months have you been saying that?

Changhyun Ahn · Hallym University Media School · October 20, 2026

We begin with the instructor’s classroom experience. Minseo, her meetings, and assignment situations are fictional examples. Actual research is identified with its sources.
지난주에 제가 여러분께 물었습니다. 설문조사 문항을 직접 만들 자신이 얼:
Last week I asked how confident you felt about writing survey questions yourselves. On a seven-point scale, what would you choose? As I remember it, more than ninety percent of roughly ten students answered two.

Two.

You are hardly strangers to AI. You use GPT and Claude, upload papers for summaries, and generate the writing you need. About half of you also completed a whole methods course last semester. Yet when I ask whether you could write a few survey items with your own hands, you are not confident.
지난주 구두 응답은 교수자 관찰·회상 · 실제 능력 점수가 아님: Instructor observation and recollection of last week’s oral responses
저는 그 대답을 듣고 수업을 어떻게 해야 하나 다시 고민했습니다. “자신:
That answer made me rethink this course. I could not simply say, ‘Have confidence,’ and move on. Nor does choosing two prove that your actual ability is two out of seven. We just learned to distinguish confidence from performance. But we do need to examine what you rely on when starting research, and where you stop.

There is something I keep hearing.

‘Professor, I am still working on my topic.’
“조금 더 정리해서 말씀드리려고요.” 바로 그 ‘조금 더’가 오늘 우리가:
‘I wanted to organize things a little more before telling you.’

That ‘a little more’ is what we need to examine. How much more must you prepare before you can come? Who decides when you are ready? If you keep preparing because you cannot make that judgment alone, will spending longer in the same place resolve it?
주제를 아직 정하지 못한 학생을 하나 놓고 생각해봅시다. 이름은 민서라고:
Let us follow a student who has not settled on a topic. We will call her Minseo. She is a fictional master's student, rather than an account of any particular person.

Minseo is interested in AI and media. Deepfakes seem concerning, misinformation seems concerning, and she wonders why people trust AI-generated content. She has plenty of interests. Turning an interest into a research topic is where she gets stuck.
교수자 설명 · 수업용 가상 사례: Instructor explanation and fictional classroom scenario
검색 결과가 많습니다. 너무 많습니다. 제목을 보면 다 내 주제와 관계가:
There are many results. Far too many. From their titles, every paper seems relevant; from their abstracts, perhaps none is. Unfamiliar theories appear, and the analysis methods are even less familiar. She opens another paper, follows its references, and soon has twenty browser tabs.

At this point she wants to ask GPT.

‘Recommend master's thesis topics about AI and misinformation.’
답이 나옵니다. 아주 그럴듯합니다. 신뢰, 리터러시, 수용 의도, 사회적:
The answer looks excellent. Trust, literacy, acceptance intention, social influence, moderation: the terms line up. Alone, she could not produce one sentence. Now she has to scroll. It feels like progress.

Yet Minseo still cannot tell which topic is feasible or what research already exists. Since she cannot judge which terms to remove, perhaps she needs them all. She asks AI for more detail. A rationale appears, then theoretical background, then hypotheses.
교수님께 보여드릴 파일은 점점 길어집니다. 설명할 자신은 이상하게 더 줄:
The file she can show her professor grows longer. Strangely, her confidence in explaining it keeps shrinking.

I understand why you use AI in this situation. Time is short. A deadline is approaching, you said the work was underway, and you need something to show. ‘Read enough and think carefully’ can be infuriating advice when no one can tell you when enough ends.
민서가 적은 첫 문장을 보겠습니다. “저는 AI와 가짜뉴스를 연구하고 싶:
Here is Minseo's first sentence.

‘I want to research AI and misinformation.’

Good: we have identified a neighborhood of interest, but not a destination. It is like saying, ‘I want to go to Seoul,’ and asking which subway to take. Where in Seoul? To a hospital, a concert, or a friend's home?
여기서 “연구문제를 구체화하세요”라고 하면 또 어렵습니다. 민서에게는 이:
‘Make your research question more specific’ may still sound difficult. I will ask Minseo this instead.

‘Which particular situation caught your attention?’

Imagine that she thinks for a moment and answers.
“같은 뉴스라도 AI가 썼다고 하면 사람들이 덜 믿을 것 같아요.” 이:
‘I think people might trust the same news less if they are told AI wrote it.’

Now we can begin a conversation. Her first sentence contained two enormous terms, AI and misinformation. This one contains someone seeing something and responding: reading news, encountering information about AI authorship, and perhaps trusting it less.
이 말을 곧바로 학술적인 문장으로 바꾸지는 마세요. “생성형 인공지능 기:
Do not rush to turn this into academic prose. Once ‘the disclosure of the production agency of generative-AI-based news content…’ starts expanding, Minseo loses her own words again. Hold on to ‘Would people trust it less if it said AI wrote it?’ for now.

But I have one question.

‘If AI wrote it, does that make it misinformation?’
아니죠. 사실을 담은 뉴스도 AI가 정리할 수 있습니다. 사람이 썼어도:
No. AI can organize factual news, and a human can write something false. Minseo started with ‘AI and misinformation,’ but her present question concerns how people interpret an authorship label, rather than whether the news itself is true.

Putting one term aside changes the search direction. Someone who kept searching for misinformation can now look for AI authorship labels, news judgments, AI-generated labels, and news accuracy.
여기서 AI를 쓰면 됩니다. 어려운 연구 제목을 더 많이 뽑아달라고 하기:
This is a useful place for AI. Rather than requesting more impressive research titles, ask it to turn your words into search terms.

‘I wonder whether people trust identical news less when it is labeled as written by AI. Suggest Korean and English search terms for relevant papers. Distinguish actual AI authorship from labeling something as AI-written. For now, give me search expressions rather than inventing paper titles or references.’

You need not memorize that prompt. The essential request is: ‘This is the situation I am curious about. What terms would researchers use to find it?’
검색어를 얻었으면 실제 검색 결과를 열어봅니다. AI가 논문을 추천했다면:
Open real search results after getting the terms. If AI recommends a paper, verify that its title and authors actually exist. If the link leads elsewhere or you cannot find the original, record that status. Just do not put an unfound paper on your list of papers read.

Even here, you can stop and ask a teacher.

‘I am interested in how an AI authorship label affects news judgments. I searched with these terms, but I am unsure whether this is the field I should enter.’
실제 논문을 한 편 열어봅시다. Altay와 Gilardi가 2024년에:
Let us open an actual paper by Altay and Gilardi, published in 2024. Even the first part of its long title could alarm Minseo: people are more skeptical of headlines labeled as AI-generated. The study reports two online experiments in the United States and United Kingdom. Original paper: Altay & Gilardi, 2024.

Minseo says:

‘Professor, they already did what I wanted to do.’
그 말이 나왔으면 지금 검색은 일을 한 겁니다. 여러분 생각이 형편없다는:
If you can say that, searching has done its job. It has not delivered a verdict that your thinking is worthless. You can now examine how someone approached a similar question.

Do not rush to either of two conclusions: ‘They did it, so I will abandon it,’ or ‘Then I will just use Korean undergraduates.’ You do not yet have enough material for either judgment. You would be discarding it, or declaring novelty, before reading.
오늘 이 논문에서 처음 확인할 것은 세상의 모든 선행연구가 아닙니다. 지:
We are not beginning with every paper in the world. First find out how far this particular study actually overlaps your question.

Open the paper, read the abstract, and find Study 1's ‘Design and procedure.’

In the PDF we obtained, it is on page 3.
여기에는 참가자가 무엇을 보고 무엇에 답했는지가 나옵니다. 연구자들은 뉴:
It explains what participants saw and what they answered.

The researchers presented news headlines and asked how accurate their claims were, or how willing participants were to share them.

In Study 1, half the participants evaluated accuracy, and the other half evaluated willingness to share.
둘 다 1부터 6까지 응답하게 했습니다. 정확성의 양끝은 ‘분명히 거짓’:
Both responses used a scale from one to six.

The accuracy endpoints correspond to definitely false and definitely true; the sharing endpoints correspond to very unlikely and very likely.

Original paper, Study 1: Design and procedure.
둘은 같은 걸까요? 여러분은 정확하다고 생각하는 뉴스를 전부 공유합니까?:
Are those the same?

Do you share every news item you consider accurate? An exchange-rate report might seem correct without belonging in your group chat. Conversely, you might share an absurd post saying, ‘Look at the nonsense going around.’ Treating sharing itself as proof of belief would already confuse the interpretation.
지난주 수업이 다시 등장했습니다. ‘좋아한다’, ‘자주 쓴다’, ‘잘할:
Last week's lesson returns. We separated liking AI, using it frequently, and feeling confident in using it. Now we separate judging accuracy and wanting to share. Survey items are not accessories suddenly attached in the methods chapter. We already need them to specify what we mean.

Minseo has not understood the whole paper. But she has a reason to revise her first sentence.

‘I wonder whether an AI authorship label affects judgments of a news headline's accuracy.’
You might say, ‘But you understand it as soon as you read it, Professor.’ True: in a familiar field, I attach new material to knowledge I already have. You are still building those attachment points. The same page inevitably takes us different amounts of time.

When I say ‘Read it yourself,’ I do not mean translating every sentence unaided and understanding every statistical formula before turning the page. Choose one question to check today, and enter the original passage that can answer it.
For example, our question now is, ‘What did this study actually ask?’ You can request this from AI.

‘In the attached paper, help me locate what participants actually saw and which questions they answered. Identify the section and a short phrase I can search in the original. Explain that passage in easy Korean. Do not infer details you cannot verify in the PDF.’
오늘은 그 문단을 확인했으면 거기까지 확인했다고 적습니다. 나머지 부분을:
Record that you checked this passage, and only that far. You need not pretend to have read the rest. Defining a reading range can also help reduce false claims about what you have read.

Perhaps you want to ask:

‘Then may I read only the useful part and ignore everything else?’
민서가 논문을 조금 읽고 AI와 다시 대화한다고 합시다. 이번에는 제법:
Suppose Minseo reads a little and returns to AI. This time an idea appears that looks more like research.

‘Instead of only labeling it AI-written, what if I also say how much the human was involved?’

For example, distinguish a journalist's article polished by AI from an article whose topic and entire text were generated by AI. Minseo is pleased: after all that reading, perhaps she has an idea of her own.
Now scroll to Study 2, on page 7 of our PDF. It already contains a related distinction. The researchers supplied different explanations of what AI use meant: polishing human-written text, drafting from provided material, or choosing a topic and writing the entire text. What varied here was the explanation of the role signified by the AI label, rather than the actual production process. Original paper, Study 2: Design and procedure.

Oh. They already did it.
여기서 “역시 저는 아이디어가 없나 봐요”로 가면 또 멈춥니다. 지금은:
If you conclude, ‘I must have no ideas,’ you stop again. This is not a verdict on your capacity for ideas. Comparing AI's novelty claim with the actual paper revealed that the paper already covered a related distinction.

Imagine discovering this after writing fifteen pages. You spend three pages asserting the study's unique contribution, then hear, ‘But this paper already did that.’ Discovering the overlap now is much more manageable than revising from that point.
AI가 “매우 독창적인 연구 주제입니다”라고 말하면 기분은 좋습니다. 하:
It feels good when AI says, ‘This is a highly original topic.’ That sentence does not substitute for a literature search. One abstract does not establish what every other paper has done. Equally, overlap in one paper does not close off your entire interest.

At this point you have a meeting question.
“저는 AI 표시의 의미를 사람들이 어떻게 이해하는지 궁금했습니다. 그런:
‘I wondered how people understand an AI label. Reading this paper, I found that Study 2 explained the label's meaning at different levels of involvement. Is this direction worth exploring further, or should I first examine responses distinct from accuracy judgments?’

The teacher can see how far you read. They may suggest another paper or advise against widening the topic yet. Even without settling the topic immediately, your next reading can change.
옵시디언을 열어봅시다. 새 플러그인을 설치하지 않아도 됩니다. 오늘은 예:
Consider opening Obsidian. You do not need another plugin, an attractive graph, or an impressive title today. A note called ‘Why might an AI label reduce belief?’ is enough.

What happens if you paste in an entire AI-generated paper summary? Next week you may reread it and ask, ‘Why did I save this?’ The distinctions you worked hard to make today may disappear inside that summary.
지금 남길 것은 이런 문장입니다. 아래는 민서가 원문을 확인하면서 적는다:
Here are the kinds of sentences to keep. This is a fictional example of what Minseo might record after checking the original.

**What first made me curious today**
I wondered whether people trust identical news less when it is labeled as AI-written.

**What I checked directly**
I checked the method of Study 1 in Altay and Gilardi's 2024 paper. Accuracy judgments and willingness to share were asked separately. My word ‘trust’ was too broad. The original location is Design and procedure, PDF page 3.
**생각이 바뀐 부분** AI 작성 표시가 뜻하는 역할을 나눠 설명하면:
**Where my thinking changed**
I thought explaining different roles signified by an AI label might be new, but Study 2 already used a related distinction. I cannot simply claim this as my contribution. The conditions appear on PDF page 7.

**What I still do not know**
I have not checked subsequent studies. I also cannot yet judge which responses beyond accuracy would be meaningful to investigate.

**What to ask my professor**
I want to ask whether I should keep reading from this paper, and which differences to examine in the next paper.
분량이 짧습니다. 하지만 이 노트에는 민서가 무엇을 알고 무엇을 모르는지:
This is short, but it reveals what Minseo knows and does not know. She can show it to a teacher or use it as context for the next AI conversation.

If you already keep paper notes, link this note to that paper's note. If links are unfamiliar, start with the paper URL and page number. Do not rebuild an entire note-management system to do this. Organizing the system must not become another day of not reading papers.
이쯤에서 민서가 묻습니다. “그래도 교수님, 논문에는 이론적 배경이 있어:
At this point Minseo asks:

‘But my thesis still needs a theoretical background, Professor. Everything so far is just my own thinking.’

So she wants AI to add relevant theories and make it academic. Theory names appear, and the writing looks impressive. Then someone asks, ‘Why is this theory needed here?’ and it becomes difficult again.
잠깐, 사람 이름과 연도를 붙이기 전에 우리말로 설명해봅시다. 왜 AI가:
Before attaching names and years, explain it in ordinary language. Why might an AI label change judgments of accuracy?

Imagine Minseo answers:

‘If AI wrote it, people might assume nobody read it before posting it.’
이제 이야기를 할 수 있습니다. ‘AI 표시를 본다’와 ‘덜 정확하다고:
Now there is something to discuss. Between seeing an AI label and judging the content less accurate, Minseo has proposed a reason: people infer a lack of human checking.

We must still investigate whether that expectation is right, whether everyone thinks that way, and how related explanations have been studied. At least we know what kind of explanation to seek. That gives us a more useful question than choosing among ten theory names supplied by AI.
“내 예상은 사람들이 AI 작성 표시를 보고 인간의 검토가 없었다고 짐작:
‘My expectation is that people may infer a lack of human review from an AI label. Suggest relevant research concepts and search terms. Do not merge different concepts as synonyms. Distinguish explanations verified in the attached paper from explanations I still need to investigate.’

That request does not finish a theoretical background. Open the original sources for the suggested concepts and check what each explains. A concept earns a place in your argument when you can explain why you chose it.
이론적 배경에서 학생이 해야 할 일은 그렇게 복잡한 말로 시작하지 않아도:
You need not begin with complicated terminology: ‘I expect this to happen for this reason, and I will examine research that supports or challenges the reason.’ Do the reading needed to sustain that sentence.

Reading may change your expectation. You might begin with ‘People simply dislike AI,’ then discover that their interpretation of what AI did matters. Your hypothesis can change too. Revise your sentences in response to reading, rather than dragging quotations into a predetermined conclusion.
When Minseo asks AI for a research model, it might produce something like the following. This is an invented classroom example, not an actual model output.

‘Generative AI literacy affects news acceptance intention through algorithmic trust, with the relationship moderated by need for cognition and technological anxiety.’

It sounds like a thesis already. Now let me ask a few questions.
AI 리터러시는 무엇입니까? AI를 자주 쓰는 겁니까, 작동 방식을 아는:
What is AI literacy: frequent use, understanding how it works, or checking its outputs? Does news acceptance mean believing, reading, or sharing? For someone with greater technological anxiety, which relationship should change, and why?

If Minseo cannot answer, she presses ‘Explain simply.’ A simple explanation appears and she can nod along. Why those variables belong in her research remains unresolved.
지금은 화살표를 하나만 남겨봅시다. 하나가 모든 연구에 정답이라는 뜻은:
Keep one arrow for now. One arrow is not the right answer for every study. We are checking the range that Minseo can explain from beginning to end.

‘For identical news headlines, an AI authorship label will produce lower accuracy evaluations than no label.’

This overlaps the study we just read. Do not submit it as Minseo's original hypothesis. We are using it to practice reading and constructing a hypothesis.
이 문장에서 비교하는 것은 표시가 있는 경우와 없는 경우입니다. 알아보려:
The comparison is between a label and no label. The response is an accuracy evaluation. The sentence also specifies an expected direction. When asked why, Minseo should distinguish evidence she read from an explanation she has not yet established.

Is ‘People with more positive attitudes toward AI will judge the news more accurate’ the same hypothesis? No. This compares people's different attitudes rather than the presence of a label. Including the word AI does not make two questions the same study.
지난주 우리 수업 이야기로 돌아오겠습니다. 여러분이 AI를 쓰고, 설문을:
Return to last week's class. Suppose you use AI and report little confidence in making a survey. What if I conclude, ‘The more AI students use, the lower their research confidence’?

First, did we measure each student's AI use together with their confidence? Watching you use AI is different from collecting paired measurements of how much each person used and what score they reported. The account we have does not even establish that the two vary together.
그럼 가상으로 자료를 모았다고 합시다. AI를 더 많이 쓰는 학생에게서:
Now imagine we collected fictional data and found lower confidence among heavier AI users. May we conclude that AI lowered their confidence?

Perhaps low confidence led to greater AI use. Perhaps harder assignments both increased AI use and reduced confidence. Several stories can fit the same observations.
Lee et al. (2025), CHI · 자기보고 조사 · doi:1: Lee et al. (2025), CHI · The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking · Self-report survey
민서에게 급한 일이 생겼다고 합시다. 다음 주까지 프로포절 15페이지를:
Suppose Minseo is suddenly told to bring a fifteen-page proposal next week. A moment ago she thought, ‘Now I know what to do.’ Now her hand reaches for GPT again.

I understand. Saying ‘There are no shortcuts to real learning’ will not move the deadline. But abandoning today's approach, generating fifteen pages, and revising all weekend can leave her entering another meeting unable to explain her own writing.
그다음 원고 전체를 처음부터 생성하기 전에, 오늘 확인한 문장을 앞에 놓:
Before generating the whole manuscript, place today's verified sentences in front of you: what you want to know, which study you actually checked, what overlaps it, and what remains undecided. This is not an exemption from fifteen pages. It is an anchor that keeps those pages from making incompatible claims.

Give AI both that anchor and the assignment requirements.
가령 연구의 필요성에 “AI 뉴스의 급증으로 전 세계 시민의 정보 판별:
Suppose its rationale begins, ‘The rapid rise of AI news is sharply reducing citizens' information-discrimination abilities worldwide.’ Where did you verify that? The paper Minseo read does not establish that enormous claim. Before polishing it, reduce it to what the evidence can actually support.

‘An AI-generated label can be a cue in evaluating content. It is useful to examine how people interpret that label.’
Nor do I want to call enduring humiliation research training. Students have a responsibility to prepare questions, and teachers have a responsibility to make the next action understandable. Graduate advising guidance also describes supervision as a shared responsibility, with mutual expectations about meetings and drafts. Cornell Graduate School, Advising Guide for Research Students, 2025.

Minseo can make the question easier to answer.
“교수님, 주제 뭐 할까요?”라고만 하면 교수님은 민서가 어디까지 와 있:
‘Professor, what should my topic be?’ does not show how far she has come. Try this instead.

‘I searched because I wondered how an AI authorship label affects accuracy judgments. I checked one paper's methods and found that a condition I thought was new was already there. I cannot judge whether to keep exploring this interest. Could you point me toward the paper or distinction I should examine next?’
이 질문을 했다고 칭찬을 보장받는 것은 아닙니다. 그래도 교수자가 고쳐줄:
This does not guarantee praise, but it gives the teacher something to correct. If they say not to judge from one paper, ask what range to examine. If the measured concept is unclear, ask which concepts need separating.

If the answer is ‘Read more papers,’ ask once more while you are there.

‘In my next reading, should I focus on types of AI labels, or should I first examine the difference between accuracy judgments and trust?’
민서가 면담을 다녀왔다고 합시다. “주제가 너무 넓다”, “그건 이미 연:
Suppose Minseo returns from a meeting after hearing, ‘The topic is too broad,’ ‘That has already been studied,’ ‘Distinguish your concepts,’ and ‘Read this paper.’ She may feel bad. But if her only note is ‘Start over,’ what will she do tomorrow?

She may ask GPT for ten new topics. Then today's discoveries disappear from the next task.
그리고 다음 작업을 작게 적습니다. “논문 공부하기”라고 쓰지 말고 “추:
Write a small next task. Instead of ‘Study papers,’ try ‘Find how the recommended paper measured trust, and place its items beside the accuracy items in the paper I already read.’ You will be able to tell when you have done it.

Add a line to the existing Obsidian note without erasing the first question: ‘Initially I grouped everything as trusting less. After the meeting, I will distinguish accuracy judgments from trust.’ Next week's you can then see why the question changed.
AI에게도 이 기록을 주면 됩니다. “지난번에 정한 방향은 이거야. 오늘:
Give that record to AI too: ‘This is the direction we chose last time. Today help with this comparison.’ That can reduce the habit of beginning every new chat with ‘Recommend a good master's thesis topic.’

Make it possible for the next task to recognize how far you have checked, rather than treating you as someone who knows nothing. Those accumulated links let your readings connect.
AI를 이용해 검색어를 만들고 실제 자료를 하나 열어봅니다. 한 편을 찾:
Use AI to develop search terms and open one real source. Finding one paper does not finalize a topic. Check where it overlaps your question. Locate one part of the methods describing what people actually did. See whether reading it changes how you express your interest.

If you cannot find it, show me the screen. Do not close it with ‘I am not ready yet.’ We can examine whether the terms are too broad, whether another field uses different language, or whether you found the paper but not the relevant passage.
자료를 찾은 분은 출처와 직접 확인한 위치를 남겨주세요. AI가 해석한:
If you found material, record the source and exact location you checked. Mark AI-only interpretations as unverified. That is today's work status, not a lifelong label of failure. It can change after you check tomorrow.

Write one question: what would you like your professor to help you judge? If you want to ask ‘Did I do well?’ divide it further. Is the question too broad? Have you distinguished two concepts? Is the study feasible with the time and material available?
지금 노트 맨 아래에 이렇게 한 문장만 먼저 써봅시다. **“교수님, 제:
Begin with one sentence at the bottom of your note.

**‘Professor, this is what I have checked so far, and this is the part I cannot judge alone.’**
오늘 따라온 과정을 자기 관심 문장이나 막힌 원고에서 이어갑니다. 스킬:
Continue the process with your own interest or a draft where you are stuck. Download the skill ZIP and the empty student Obsidian vault, then follow the getting-started guide.

The Advisor finds actual papers, narrows what to read, and records what you explained and what remains unknown. It does not count AI’s explanations as knowledge the student already possesses.
“제가 궁금한 것은 ○○입니다. 지금 확인한 것은 여기까지이고, 이 부분:
“I am curious about ○○. This is what I have checked, and this is what I cannot explain. Ask me questions and help me find the original passages I need to read myself.”

You do not need a finished proposal to begin. Bring an initial interest, a passage where reading stopped, or feedback from your advisor.

AI가 써준 원고와 내가 설명할 수 있는 연구 사이에서, 다음에 할 일을: This class helps you find the next step between an AI-written draft and research you can explain yourself.
민서는 가상의 석사생입니다. 실제 논문과 교수자의 경험은 각각 구분해 표: Minseo is a fictional master's student. Actual research and the instructor's experience are labelled separately.
지난주, 7점 중 2점이라고 했습니다: Last week, you said two out of seven
GPT와 클로드로 논문을 요약하고 글을 만들어봅니다. 지난 학기에 방법론: You summarize papers and draft text with GPT and Claude. About half of you also took a full methods course last semester.
그런데 설문 문항을 내 손으로 만들 자신이 얼마나 있느냐고 물으면 대답이: But ask how confident you are that you can write survey items yourself, and the answer changes. As I recall, more than 90% of roughly ten students said two on a seven-point scale.
자신감이 2점이라고 실제 능력도 2점이라고 단정할 수는 없습니다. 지난주: Confidence of two does not establish that actual ability is also two. Last week, we distinguished liking, use, and confidence.
다만 “자신감을 가지세요”라고 넘어갈 수도 없습니다. 연구를 시작할 때: Still, we cannot simply say, “Be confident,” and move on. We need to examine what you rely on when beginning research and where you get stuck.
계속 잡으러 다니는데 얼굴을 못 봅니다: You keep hunting for a topic without ever seeing it
처음 “주제를 잡고 있어요”라고 하면 그럴 수 있습니다. 관심 분야를 둘: The first time you say, “I am still finding a topic,” that can make sense. You may be exploring an area or changing your mind as you read.
한 달 뒤에도, 다음 학기에도 같은 말이면 이야기가 달라집니다. 석사 2: If you say the same thing a month later or next semester, it is a different story. You are in your second or third master's semester and still finding it.
자료를 찾고 AI에게 물어봤다는 것은 압니다. 그래서 지난번과 비교해 무: I know you searched for materials and asked AI. But ask what you learned since last time, and you say, “Once I organize it a little more…”
“조금 더 준비해서”는 언제 끝납니까?: When does “a little more preparation” end?
“빈손으로 찾아가기는 미안합니다. 논문을 조금 더 읽고, 생각을 정리해서: “I feel bad visiting empty-handed. I want to read a few more papers and organize my thoughts before I speak to you.”
그런데 몇 편을 읽어야 하는지, 무엇을 정리해야 하는지, 준비가 됐는지를: But you cannot decide alone how many papers are enough, what needs organizing, or whether you are ready.
한 달 뒤에도, 다음 학기에도 같은 말을 합니다. 혼자 판단이 안 돼서: A month later, and next semester, you say the same thing. If you keep preparing because you cannot judge this alone, will spending more time in the same place solve it?
교수자가 함께 볼 수 있는 것: What an instructor can examine with you
“이 검색어로 찾아봤는데 제 분야가 맞는지 모르겠습니다. 이 문단을 읽었: “I searched with these terms, but I do not know whether this is my field. I read this paragraph, but I cannot explain it from here onward.”
완성된 제목이 없어도 됩니다. 어디까지 했고 어디에서 막혔는지가 보이면,: You do not need a finished title. If we can see what you did and where you got stuck, we can decide the next step together.
오늘 바꿀 것은 멋진 제목보다 도움을 요청할 문장입니다. 무엇을 모르는지: Today, we are improving the sentence you use to ask for help before polishing an impressive title. Showing what you do not know gives us material for deciding what to do next.
막힌 자리에서 다음 작업으로 갑니다: Move from the sticking point to the next task
논문 제목부터 만들지 않습니다. 무엇을 보고 어떤 생각이 들었는지 자기: Do not start by generating a paper title. Describe in your own words what you saw and what it made you wonder.
실제 논문 한 편에서 내가 궁금한 것과 겹치는 부분을 찾아봅니다. 읽은: Find the part of an actual paper that overlaps with your question. Record only what you have read.
이론·가설·방법을 붙이기 전에, 같은 단어를 무엇의 뜻으로 썼는지 확인합: Before adding theory, hypotheses, or methods, check what you mean when you use the same word.
아직 결정하지 못한 것을 교수자가 함께 판단할 수 있게 보여줍니다. 면담: Show what remains undecided in a form your instructor can help assess. Decide what to read next after the meeting.
가상의 석사생 민서를 따라가봅시다: Follow Minseo, a fictional master's student
관심은 많은데, 연구로 바꾸는 곳에서 멈춥니다: Plenty of interests; stuck turning them into research
민서는 AI와 미디어에 관심이 있습니다. 딥페이크도 문제 같고, 가짜뉴스: Minseo is interested in AI and media. Deepfakes seem problematic, fake news seems problematic, and people's trust in AI content is interesting too.
교수님을 찾아가야 한다는 것은 압니다. “그래서 뭘 하고 싶은데?”라는: Minseo knows it is time to visit the professor. But without confidence about answering “What do you want to do?”, Minseo searches for more papers first.
제목은 다 관련 있어 보이고, 초록을 읽으면 관계가 없는 것 같기도 합니: Every title looks relevant, yet some abstracts seem unrelated. Unfamiliar theories and methods send Minseo from tab to tab.
파일은 길어지고 자신은 없어집니다: The file gets longer; confidence gets lower
교수님께 갈 때 뭔가 있어야 할 것 같습니다. 몇 편이면 충분한지는 모르: It feels as though there must be something to show the professor. Without knowing how many papers are enough, Minseo starts searching.
이론도 방법도 낯섭니다. 한 편을 읽다가 다른 논문을 열고, 어느새 탭이: Both theory and methods are unfamiliar. Reading one paper leads to opening another; soon there are twenty tabs.
“주제 추천해줘.” 신뢰·리터러시·조절효과가 줄을 섭니다. 제목도 가설도: “Suggest a topic.” Trust, literacy, and moderation effects line up. There are titles and hypotheses now; it feels like progress.
무엇이 가능한지, 무엇을 빼야 하는지는 여전히 모릅니다. 설명할 자신이: Minseo still does not know what is feasible or what to cut. Without confidence about explaining the draft, Minseo asks AI to write more.
민서가 AI를 계속 쓰는 이유를 압니다: I understand why Minseo keeps using AI
“충분히 읽고 천천히 생각하세요”라고 하면 속이 터질 수 있습니다. 충분: “Read enough and think carefully” can be maddening when you do not even know when “enough” ends.
교수님께 진행 중이라고 말씀드렸고, 뭔가 보여드려야 합니다. 파일을 길게: You told your professor that work was underway, and you must show something. Making the file longer looks like a solution you can actually grasp.
그래서 다음 판단을 작게 만듭니다: So we make the next decision smaller
AI를 쓰지 말라는 말로 끝내지 않겠습니다. 무엇을 물어보고, 어디를 직: We will not stop at telling you not to use AI. We will separate what to ask, where to check for yourself, and which question to bring.
교수자도 “더 생각해오세요”에서 멈추면 안 됩니다. 학생이 다음에 할 행: Instructors must also go beyond “Think about it some more.” They need to help students recognize the next action.
AI와 가짜뉴스도 아직은 넓은 주소입니다: “AI and fake news” is still a broad address
“저는 AI와 가짜뉴스를 연구하고 싶습니다.” 관심 있는 동네는 말했습니: “I want to study AI and fake news.” You have named a neighborhood of interest. What you will actually do is still unclear.
서울에 간다면서 지하철 몇 호선을 타야 하냐고 묻는 것과 비슷합니다. 회: It is like asking which subway line to take because you are going to Seoul. The route depends on whether you are going to work or to a concert.
이때 “연구문제를 구체화하세요”라고만 하면 또 어렵습니다. 먼저 묻겠습니: Simply saying “Make your research question specific” is still hard. Let me ask first: which particular situation caught your attention?
학술 용어보다 장면이 먼저입니다: A concrete situation comes before academic terminology
민서가 실제로 궁금한 것: What Minseo actually wants to know
같은 뉴스가 있고, AI가 썼다는 정보가 붙고, 사람이 다르게 판단할 것: There is the same news story, a label saying AI wrote it, and an expectation that people will judge it differently. Now we can see what you want to compare.
벌써 어렵게 쓰지 마세요: Do not make it difficult already
“생성형 인공지능 기반 정보 수용자의 인지적…”으로 고치면 민서는 다시: If the sentence becomes “The cognitive characteristics of recipients of generative-AI-based information…”, Minseo loses their own words again.
우선 “AI가 썼다고 하면 덜 믿을까?”를 다듬으면 됩니다. 용어는 그: Start by refining “Will people believe it less if they are told AI wrote it?” Add terminology to explain the situation, not to obscure it.
AI가 썼다는 것과 가짜라는 것은 다릅니다: Written by AI does not mean false
정확한 내용을 AI가 쓸 수도 있고, 사람이 쓴 내용이 틀릴 수도 있습니: AI can write accurate content, and content written by a person can be wrong.
Do not treat AI authorship and factual truth as the same thing.
같은 내용이라도 AI가 썼다는 표시를 본 사람이 다르게 판단할 수 있습니: Even with identical content, seeing a label that says AI wrote it may change a person's judgment.
Minseo's question is closer to how people interpret that label.
AI 작성 표시, 정확성 판단, AI-generated label, ne: Try terms for AI authorship labels and accuracy judgments, including “AI-generated label” and “news accuracy.”
You may find different research than a search for “fake news” alone would produce.

Changing every sentence to “The higher X, the higher Y” does not make it science. You still need to explain why you expect that direction.
독립변인·종속변인이라는 이름을 외워도 비교할 장면이 보이지 않으면 설계는: Memorizing “independent variable” and “dependent variable” will not resolve the design if you cannot picture the comparison.
아직 방향을 정하기 어렵다면: If the direction is still hard to specify
“어떤 차이가 있는가?”라는 연구문제로 두고 지도교수와 상의할 수도 있습: You may keep “What differences are there?” as a research question and discuss it with your advisor. Not all research requires the same form of causal hypothesis.
먼저 무엇을 보여주고 무엇을 물으며 어떤 답을 비교할지 정리합니다. 그다: First describe what you would show, ask, and compare. There is time to add the necessary terminology afterward.
여러분이 AI를 쓰는 모습을 봤고, 설문을 만들 자신감은 낮게 답했습니다: I saw you using AI, and you reported low confidence about creating a survey. That much is the instructor's experience.
하지만 학생별로 누가 얼마나 쓰고, 그 학생이 몇 점을 답했는지를 짝지어: But we do not currently have paired data identifying how much each student used AI and which confidence score that same student gave.
자료 없이 넘어가면 안 되는 것: What we cannot claim without data
“AI를 많이 쓸수록 자신감이 낮다”는 말은 두 값이 함께 움직였다는 주: “More AI use means less confidence” claims that two values vary together. An observational impression alone is not enough to say that.
먼저 사용량과 자신감을 함께 측정했는지부터 봐야 합니다. 상관과 인과를: First check whether use and confidence were measured together. Before separating correlation from causation, establish whether the relationship itself was examined.
관계가 보여도 원인은 아직 남아 있습니다: Even with a relationship, causation remains unresolved
이번에는 가상 자료가 있다고 합시다: Suppose this time we have fictional data
학생별 AI 사용량과 자신감을 모았습니다. 많이 쓰는 학생에게서 자신감이: We collected each student's AI use and confidence. Students with higher use reported lower confidence.
이제 관계를 살펴볼 자료는 생겼습니다. 그래도 “AI가 자신감을 떨어뜨렸: Now we have data for examining a relationship. We still cannot jump straight to “AI reduced their confidence.”
같은 자료에 다른 설명이 붙습니다: The same data allow other explanations
자신감이 낮아서 AI를 더 많이 썼을 수 있습니다. 어려운 과제가 AI: Low confidence may have led to more AI use. A difficult assignment may have increased AI use and reduced confidence.
다른 설명을 구별하려고 먼저 일어난 일, 비교 대상, 함께 바뀐 조건을: To distinguish explanations, examine what happened first, the comparison group, and conditions that changed together. Adding “effect” to every hypothesis skips this work.
피곤하면 커피를 압수하면 됩니까?: Should we confiscate coffee when people are tired?
가상 조사에서 커피를 많이 마신 사람이 더 피곤하다고 답했습니다. 그 응: In a fictional survey, people who drank more coffee reported greater tiredness. Those responses alone cannot settle which of the following stories is correct.
같은 관찰에 붙는 이야기: A story consistent with the same observation
Coffee may have disrupted sleep and increased tiredness.
Check which came first: coffee or tiredness.
People who were already tired may have sought more coffee to keep going.
Examine tiredness before drinking and the reason for seeking coffee.
A deadline may have caused both less sleep and more coffee consumption.
Check whether another condition could change both responses.
뉴스도 표시도 다르면 무엇 때문입니까?: If both the news and the label differ, which caused the difference?
구분하려는 비교: A comparison designed to separate the difference
A집단에는 한 뉴스, B집단에는 다른 뉴스를 보여줍니다. 표시도 서로 다: Group A sees one story and group B another. Their labels differ too.
For the classroom exercise, imagine the same content with different labels.
If people choose whichever condition they want, differences between people may be mixed in.
Consider a design that randomly assigns which condition participants see.
Even if scores differ, it is difficult to explain whether the content or the label accounts for it.
어떤 차이를 더 잘 따져볼 수 있는지 봅니다. 실제 설계의 준비는 더 필: Consider which difference the design lets you examine more clearly. Preparing an actual design still requires further work.
무작위 배정이면 준비가 끝납니까?: Does random assignment finish the preparation?
참가자가 표시를 보았습니까? 문구를 의도대로 이해합니까? 뉴스가 비교에: Did participants see the label? Do they understand the wording as intended? Is the news suitable for the comparison?
필요한 참여자를 구할 수 있습니까? 지도와 연구윤리 절차를 확인했습니까?: Can you recruit the necessary participants? Have you checked supervision and research ethics procedures? Do not start distributing a link based on a practice design.
“제 질문은 한 번 설문으로 물어봐도 되는지, 표시를 다르게 보여주는 비: “I cannot judge whether a one-time survey is enough for my question or whether I need a comparison showing different labels.”
전문가는 쓰는 동안 계속 판단합니다: Experts keep judging as they write
분야를 아는 사람이 AI를 쓸 때: When someone who knows the field uses AI
출력된 문장에서 약한 근거, 이미 있는 연구, 필요 없는 이론, 가진 자: They recognize weak evidence, existing studies, unnecessary theories, and comparisons their data cannot support in the generated text.
화면에서는 AI가 다 써준 것처럼 보여도 그 사람은 계속 선택하고 버리고: On screen, AI may seem to write everything, but the person keeps choosing, discarding, and revising. Background knowledge supports that work.
초심자가 같은 일을 맡길 때: When a beginner assigns the same task
어떤 주제가 독창적인지, 가능한지, 지도교수에게 설명할 수 있는지까지 한: They may ask AI all at once which topic is original, feasible, and explainable to their advisor.
결과를 열심히 읽어도 어디부터 검수할지 모르겠습니다. 성의가 부족해서만이: Even after diligently reading the output, they do not know where to begin checking. It is not only a lack of effort; too many judgments requiring verification have accumulated.
교수자 설명 / Lee et al. (2025), CHI · 자기보고 조: Instructor explanation / Lee et al. (2025), CHI · Self-report survey
AI 둘이 맞다는데 확인은 끝났습니까?: Two AIs agree. Is the checking finished?
GPT에게 “이거 맞아?”라고 물었더니 맞다고 합니다. 다른 AI도 맞다: You ask GPT, “Is this right?” and it agrees. Another AI agrees too. Both models may have produced the same plausible explanation.
모델끼리 동의했다는 사실이 논문의 실제 문장, 측정 내용, 결과 또는 내: Agreement between models does not verify the actual wording of a paper, its measures or findings, or the feasibility of your study.
확인할 수 있는 크기로 맡깁니다: Assign work at a size you can check
검색어 바꾸기, 읽을 문단 찾기, 어려운 문장 풀기, 두 문장에서 같은: Rephrasing search terms, locating passages, explaining difficult sentences, and finding inconsistent uses of a word across two sentences can help.
작업이 작으면 결과를 원문과 비교할 위치가 보입니다. AI를 덜 쓰라는: A small task makes it easier to see where to compare the result with the original. The point is to divide work according to what you can judge, rather than simply use AI less.
Lee 등의 2025년 연구에서 볼 점: What to examine in Lee et al.'s 2025 study
생성형 AI를 사용하는 지식노동자 319명의 설문과 업무 사례를 분석했습: The researchers analyzed survey responses and work examples from 319 knowledge workers using generative AI. This was not an experiment on graduate students.
AI에 대한 자신감, 자신의 과업 수행 자신감, 비판적으로 검토했다고 보: The study examined relationships among confidence in AI, confidence in one's own task performance, and reported critical evaluation behavior. It also discusses time pressure and difficulty reviewing unfamiliar domains.
자기보고 조사입니다. ‘AI가 대학원생의 지능을 떨어뜨렸다’는 인과 실험: This is a self-report survey, not a causal experiment establishing that AI reduced graduate students' intelligence. It helps us consider why reviewing requires time and knowledge too.
이해했어도 제출일은 그대로입니다: Understanding does not change the deadline
방금까지는 “이렇게 해야겠구나” 했는데 손이 다시 GPT로 갑니다. “진: A moment ago you thought, “Now I see what to do,” but your hand reaches for GPT again. Saying “There is no shortcut to real learning” does not move the deadline.
그렇다고 15페이지를 먼저 생성하고 주말 내내 고치는 방식으로 돌아가면,: Yet if you return to generating fifteen pages first and editing all weekend, you may again arrive at a meeting unable to explain your own draft.
첫 작업은 제출 조건을 꺼내는 일입니다: Start by bringing out the submission requirements
필수 목차, 참고문헌의 분량 포함 여부, 탐색 중인 계획도 가능한지, 어: Check the required sections, whether references count toward the page limit, whether an exploratory plan is acceptable, and which part the feedback is meant to address.
이미 받은 안내가 있으면 다시 물을 필요 없이 꺼냅니다. 형식이 정해졌다: If instructions already exist, retrieve them instead of asking again. Follow an established format. Do not let AI invent submission requirements that were never given.
이 기록은 15페이지를 대신하는 면제권이 아닙니다. 각 장에서 서로 다른: This record is not an exemption from writing fifteen pages. It is a reference that keeps different chapters from saying different things.
AI 작성 표시가 뉴스 제목의 정확성 판단에 어떤 차이를 만드는지 궁금하: I wonder how an AI-written label changes accuracy judgments of news headlines.
연구 1의 측정 구분과 연구 2의 표시 설명 조건을 확인했다. 내가 생각: I checked the distinction between measures in Study 1 and the label-explanation conditions in Study 2. The difference I had in mind overlaps with what has already been studied.
어떤 추가 질문이 의미 있는지, 내 여건에서 어떤 비교가 가능한지 아직: I have not yet judged which additional question is meaningful or which comparison is feasible in my circumstances. I record the materials and guidance I need.
AI에게 줄 기준을 문장으로 씁니다: Write down the basis you will give AI
한꺼번에 맡기면: If you assign everything at once
“Write a fifteen-page proposal on an original, feasible topic my professor will like.”
연구의 새로움, 자료의 적합성, 설계의 실행 가능성, 지도 방향을 모두: This hands over novelty, data suitability, design feasibility, and supervisory direction while all of them remain difficult for you to assess.
확인한 내용으로 시작하면: If you start with what you checked
“아래는 원문에서 확인한 내용과 아직 결정하지 못한 것이야. 과제 목차의: “Below are what I checked in the original and what remains undecided. First suggest where they belong in the assignment's outline.”
“근거가 없는 곳은 그럴듯하게 채우지 말고 필요한 자료를 표시해줘. 참고: “Where evidence is missing, identify the material needed instead of filling the gap plausibly. Do not invent references. Let us draft the parts that can be written from what I checked.”
“아직 모름”을 확신처럼 쓰지 마세요: Do not turn “I do not know yet” into certainty
긴 초안을 한꺼번에 받기 전에 한 문단부터 봅니다. 내가 확인한 근거와: Examine one paragraph before requesting a long draft all at once. Find where your checked evidence and question appear.
AI가 ‘아직 모른다’를 확정적인 문장으로 바꾸거나, 읽지 않은 연구를: Check whether AI turned “not yet known” into a confident statement or added unread research as though it were evidence.
주장을 뒷받침할 수 있는 범위로 줄입니다. 미확인 부분은 필요한 자료나: Narrow the claim to what you can support. Leave unchecked parts as needed sources or unresolved decisions.
검토한 문단을 기준으로 다음 문단을 만듭니다. 같은 단어와 같은 연구 질: Use the reviewed paragraph as the basis for the next one. Check again that the same words and research question remain consistent.
첫 문단에 온 세상을 넣지 마세요: Do not put the whole world in your opening paragraph
“AI 뉴스의 급증으로 전 세계 시민의 정보 판별 능력이 급격히 저하되고: “The surge in AI news is rapidly eroding citizens' ability to assess information around the world.”
어디서 확인했습니까? 민서가 읽은 논문은 그런 거대한 문장 전체를 입증하: Where did you verify that? The paper Minseo read was not evidence for that entire sweeping statement. Examine the scope before making it sound impressive.
지금 출발할 수 있는 문장: A sentence you can start from now
Then describe specifically what the relevant research observed and under which conditions. Starting broadly is not a requirement for academic writing.
미확인 표시를 지우면 해결됩니까?: Does deleting the “unchecked” marker solve anything?
모르는 부분과 필요한 자료를 표시해도 됩니다. 어디가 미완성인지 알아야: You can mark what you do not know and which materials are needed. Knowing what is unfinished helps you decide what to read and ask next.
하지만 제출 전에 표시만 지우고 확정된 사실처럼 쓰면, 모르는 부분을 해: But deleting the markers before submission and writing as though everything were established hides the unknowns instead of resolving them.
확인해서 쓸 수 있는 주장만 남기거나, 계획에서 결정이 필요한 부분이라고: Keep only claims you can verify and support, explain which parts of the plan still require decisions, or discuss a feasible scope within the deadline.
일주일에 전문가의 지식을 따라잡거나 교수님의 반응을 보장할 수는 없습니다: You cannot acquire an expert's knowledge in a week or guarantee your professor's reaction. Still, a draft distinguishing checked evidence from remaining work gives you a next step that an entirely unexplained draft cannot.
그 부담을 의지 문제로만 보지 않습니다: I do not reduce that burden to willpower
제가 “안 혼내니까 바로 물어보세요”라고 해도 모든 연구실의 분위기가 같: I may say, “Ask right away; I will not scold you,” but not every research group has the same atmosphere. A professor's remark can substantially change a student's behavior.
상처를 견디는 능력을 연구 훈련이라고 부르고 싶지는 않습니다. 학생이 질: I do not want to call enduring hurt “research training.” If students prepare questions, instructors also have a responsibility to help them recognize what to do next.
그래도 지금 할 수 있는 일을 찾습니다: Still, look for what you can do now
지도 관계의 기대를 함께 확인하도록 권하는 대학원 안내도 있습니다. 상담: Graduate advising guides also recommend clarifying expectations together. Knowing meeting frequency, the expected state of drafts, and the purpose of feedback makes the burden of seeking help more concrete.
질문을 가져가면 반드시 칭찬받는다는 약속은 하지 않겠습니다. 다만 무엇을: I will not promise that bringing a question guarantees praise. But you can prepare material that makes it possible to see what needs revision.
가상 면담 예시 / Cornell Graduate School, Advi: Fictional advising example / Cornell Graduate School, Advising Guide (2025)
교수자가 고쳐줄 대상을 보여주세요: Show something your instructor can help revise
관심 분야만 말하면 교수자는 학생이 무엇을 알아봤고, 어떤 판단을 도와줘: If you state only an area of interest, an instructor cannot easily tell what you have investigated or which judgment needs help.
“좀 더 읽어보세요”라는 답을 듣고 돌아와도 다음에 무엇을 읽을지는 여전: Even after hearing “Read a little more,” you may still have no idea what to read next.
질문을 잘하면 칭찬받는다는 약속은 아닙니다. 교수님의 반응이 두려운 현실: A well-prepared question does not guarantee praise. Fear of a professor's reaction is real. Still, a question with something concrete to revise leaves material for the next conversation.
“AI 표시가 정확성 판단에 주는 영향이 궁금합니다. 이 논문의 방법을: “I am interested in how AI labels affect accuracy judgments. I examined this paper's methods and discovered that the condition I thought was new already exists.”
“이 관심을 유지하면서 더 볼 가치가 있는지 어렵습니다. 다음에 확인할: “I find it difficult to judge whether this interest is worth pursuing further. Could you point me to the next concept or paper to examine?”
“이미 있는 연구다”라고 하시면 겹치는 논문을, “개념이 불분명하다”라고: If the response is “That research already exists,” you can examine the overlapping paper together. If it is “Your concept is unclear,” you can look at the confusing sentence.
“더 읽으라”면 무엇을 볼지 묻습니다: If told to read more, ask what to look for
방향 없이 받아오면: If you return without a direction
노트에는 “논문 더 읽기”가 남습니다. 다음 주에도 어떤 논문에서 무엇을: Your note says “Read more papers.” Next week, you may stop at the search box again, unsure which paper to read or what to check.
It is better not to assume you already understood the professor's meaning precisely. Check once more what you should compare.
그 자리에서 이렇게 물을 수 있습니다: You can ask on the spot
“다음 논문에서는 AI 표시의 종류를 비교하는 데 집중하면 될까요? 아니: “Should I focus on comparing types of AI labels in the next paper, or first examine the difference between accuracy judgments and trust?”
내가 잘못 잡았다면 바로잡을 수 있습니다. 다른 방향을 권하시면 다음 읽: If you misunderstood, it can be corrected. A different recommended direction changes your next reading. Bringing back a next task matters more than merely finishing the meeting.
만나기 어려우면 연락 방식부터 확인합니다: If meeting is difficult, clarify how to communicate
짧은 글로 질문해도 되는지, 예약해 면담해야 하는지, 전체 원고보다 일부: Check whether short written questions are acceptable, whether you need an appointment, and whether you may show a section rather than an entire draft.
교수자가 선호하는 방식을 알면 “언제 무엇을 가져가야 하나”의 부담을 조: Knowing an instructor's preferred approach helps make the burden of “When should I bring what?” more concrete.
과목 담당 교수나 선배에게 논문 읽는 방법을 물을 수 있습니다. 다만 최: You can ask a course instructor or senior student how to read papers. But the final topic and research direction need to be confirmed within the advising relationship. Continue reading and recording while you wait.
이 말을 잘 준비하려고 또 한 달 버티지 마세요. 논문을 못 찾은 검색어: Do not spend another month preparing this sentence perfectly. The search terms that failed or the paragraph you could not understand can be shown now.
면담하고 왔는데 “혼났다”만 남았습니까?: Did the meeting leave only “I got scolded”?
다시 해야 함, 그다음에는 무엇을 합니까?: “Redo it.” What do you do after that?
“주제가 넓다”, “이미 연구가 있다”, “개념을 구분하라”, “더 읽어: Hearing “The topic is broad,” “Research already exists,” “Distinguish the concepts,” or “Read more” may leave you feeling bad.
노트에 “다시 해야 함”만 적으면 다음 날 GPT에게 처음부터 주제를 다: If your only note is “Redo it,” you may ask GPT for topics from scratch the next day. What you checked this time does not connect to the next task.
교수님이 실제로 한 말과 내가 이해한 뜻을 나눠 적습니다. 틀리게 이해했: Separate what the professor actually said from what you understood it to mean. Record it in a form you can check if you misunderstood.
교수님의 말, 내 해석, 다음 행동을 나눕니다: Separate the professor's words, your interpretation, and the next action
“정확성 판단과 신뢰를 구분해보세요.” 실제로 받은 피드백을 먼저 적습니: “Distinguish accuracy judgments from trust.” Record the actual feedback first.
“두 개념의 측정 문항을 비교해보라는 뜻으로 이해했다.” 교수님의 말과: “I understood this as a request to compare the measurement items for the two concepts.” Do not assume in advance that your interpretation matches the professor's words.
“논문에서 두 개념을 어떻게 물었는지 비교해서 가져오면 될까요?” 이해가: “Should I compare how the two concepts were measured in the papers and bring that?” If uncertain, confirm briefly through the preferred communication channel.
끝이 보이는 읽기 과제를 적습니다: Write a reading task with a visible endpoint

Explore existing and new capabilities across 39 diagram groups and 104 actual examples, alongside the original atlas of 18 recipes, 47 states, and editorial compositions.
도표 유형을 고르고, 원본·데이터·출력·검증 결과까지 확인하려는 연구자·: Researchers, educators, and creators choosing diagram types and checking their sources, data, outputs, and validation evidence.
전체 도식 검토실은 Pele 1.6.0의 콘텐츠 문법 32개와 Achma:
The complete collection organizes 32 content grammars from Pele 1.6.0 and seven additional Achmage diagram groups into 39 independent pages. Its 104 actual examples comprise 32 grammar examples, 47 states from the original 18 recipes, 18 conditions across nine statistical analysis families, six editorial contexts, and one JSON data-binding example. Clickable marks, colors, viewport widths, and analysis conditions do not count as additional diagram types.

Each example provides its source input, data table, renderer attribution, SVG and PNG outputs, and known limitations. The workbench demonstrates updates, error recovery, selection persistence, and font changes. The Hangul integration includes a new document, a text edit, and a diagram replacement. All examples in the new collection use synthetic data.

The collection was checked across 624 screen conditions: 104 examples at three viewport widths in light and dark themes. Eight lifecycle checks, 11 project-update and conflict checks, and nine numerical cross-checks also passed. Automated screen checks are distinguished from human visual review. Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, Obsidian, and saving and reopening in the Ieum app remain unverified. Korean Sankey, small Treemap items, and XY labels retain documented limitations.

The full collection is currently an owner-only GPT Site. It requires the owner's ChatGPT sign-in and is not presented as a demo open to every visitor. The original atlas and the 18 social-science slides with their production code remain publicly available below. Existing presentation URLs and pinned engine versions are preserved.
